quick.intro: Not every night ends in a restaurant. These are places near each hotel that are still open when you get back late. Check the closing time before you set off.

till.title: At the till, and on the way out
lines: 🔴 The cashier asks whether you are eating in the shop. Your answer sets the tax: 10% to eat in, 8% to take away. It cannot be changed after you pay. If you say takeaway, take the food away.

You will also be asked “atatamemasu ka?” (温めますか？), which means “Shall I heat it?”. Say hai (はい) for yes, or daijōbu desu (だいじょうぶです) for no. You are asked separately whether you want chopsticks, and they are handed to you at the counter.

🔴 Supermarkets mark food down three times a day. Around 16:00–17:00: 10–20% off. Around 19:00–20:00: 20–30% off. From 1–2 hours before closing: 30% off, up to half price. Bento, lunch plates and sushi are also marked down at about 14:00–16:00.
⚑ When rain is forecast, the markdowns start earlier, because shoppers come in earlier.
⚠ There are almost no bins on Japanese streets. Shops have a bin by the counter or the door. Use it before you leave, or you will carry the packaging back to the hotel.

bases.title: Tokyo — Akihabara
bases.note: 🔴 Back late? Yoshinoya (beef bowls), 250 m up Shōwa-dōri, is open until 02:00. Later than that: Hanamasa supermarket is open 24 hours, but it sells mostly meat and groceries and few ready-made meals. Jonathan’s and Sukiya (open until 03:00) and Coco’s (until 04:00) are listed under Balanced meals. Life supermarket is open until 24:00 for a boxed meal to eat cold. Supermarkets mark food down 1–2 hours before closing, so at Life the cheapest time is about 22:00–23:00. ⚠ The hotel has no microwave listed, so you can't heat it up.

options.name_jp: 吉野家 秋葉原店
options.walk: ≈250 m — about 4 minutes, on the Shōwa-dōri side
options.what: Beef-over-rice bowls, ready in a minute or two. Table seating, or takeaway from the same counter.
options.address_jp: 〒101-0023 東京都千代田区神田松永町10-1
options.note: ⚑ Open until 02:00, so it still works after a very late return.

options.name_jp: ライフ 神田和泉町店
options.what: A full supermarket with a counter that makes prepared food on site: bento, fried dishes, sushi packs and bread. It is the biggest supermarket within walking distance of the hotel.
options.address_jp: 〒101-0024 東京都千代田区神田和泉町2-13
options.note: 🔴 The biggest supermarket near the hotel that is open late. It closes at midnight, so its biggest discounts (30% off, up to half price) start at about 22:00.

options.name_jp: ほっともっと 岩本町店
options.what: Hot bento cooked to order: karaage (fried chicken), ginger pork, katsu-don. No seating. It is cooked while you wait, so allow 10 minutes.
options.address_jp: 〒101-0032 東京都千代田区岩本町2-8-10
options.note: Takes cards, IC cards such as Suica, and QR-code payment apps.

options.name_jp: 肉のハナマサ 秋葉原店
options.what: A supermarket run by a wholesale butcher, open to the public. ⚠ It is strongest on meat and groceries, and it has fewer ready-made bento than Life supermarket.
options.address_jp: 東京都台東区秋葉原4-14
options.note: ⚑ Open 24 hours, so it is still open at 03:00.

options.name_jp: デニーズ 秋葉原中央口店
options.hours: ⚠ Not confirmed: either open 24 hours or 06:30–23:00. Check as you pass, and do not plan around it.
options.walk: In the hotel building — 2F, same address
options.what: Sit-down family restaurant: rice plates, pasta, breakfast sets, drink bar.
options.address_jp: 東京都千代田区神田佐久間町1-8-3 ダイハツ秋葉原ビル2F
options.note: ⚑ It is on the 2nd floor of the hotel building. Check its hours as you come in on the first night.

bases.title: Kyoto — Kyoto Station
bases.note: 🔴 Late meal at the hotel: the Dormy Inn serves a free bowl of ramen every night, 21:30–23:00. That covers every late return from Nara and Yoshino. ⚠ The supermarket and the 24-hour Yoshinoya are both on the Hachijō (south) side of the station, so allow time to walk through or under it.

options.name_jp: 夜鳴きそば
options.what: A small bowl of light soy-sauce (shōyu) ramen, free for guests. Also free: ice lollies on 9F, 15:00–01:00, and a lactic drink on 9F, 05:00–10:00. The bath is open 15:00–10:00. Breakfast is 06:30–09:30, last entry 09:00.
options.note: 🔴 You stay here 10 of the 20 nights, so this is the most useful late-night food on the trip. On the Nara days, the planned trains get you back before 21:30, so the ramen is there later in the evening. ⚠ The hotel lists no microwave in the rooms or on the floors, only a laundry on 9F and vending machines on 2F, 5F and 9F. Do not count on heating a supermarket meal here.

options.name_jp: 京都ポルタ おみやげ街道
options.hours: Omiyage Kaidō 07:30–22:00 · Porta Dining 11:00–22:00 · B1 café 07:00–23:00 · drugstore 07:00–22:00
options.walk: ≈335 m — under the station, indoors most of the way
options.what: Boxed bento and Kyoto prepared food, plus sit-down restaurants, in the underground mall directly in front of the station.
options.address_jp: 京都市下京区東塩小路町902
options.note: ⚑ The nearest place to buy food late on the hotel’s side of the station. ⚠ B1 shops close at 20:30 and B2 shops at 20:00. After 20:30, only Omiyage Kaidō, Porta Dining, the B1 café and the drugstore are still open. The pin marks the mall entrance; the shops are underground below it.

options.name_jp: マーケットガーデンKOHYO イオンモールKYOTO店
options.walk: ≈835 m straight line — Hachijō side, so allow 15 minutes through the station
options.what: A full supermarket on the ground floor of the Aeon Mall, with the usual prepared-food and bento counters.
options.address_jp: 京都市南区西九条鳥居口町1 イオンモールKYOTO 1F
options.note: ⚠ The only real supermarket near the hotel, and it is on the opposite side of the station from the hotel. It closes at 22:00, so its biggest discounts start at about 20:00–21:00. The pin marks the Aeon Mall; KOHYO is on its ground floor.

options.name_jp: 吉野家 京都八条口店
options.what: Beef bowls, with table seating or takeaway. Open 24 hours.
options.address_jp: 〒601-8411 京都府京都市南区西九条北ノ内町41-4
options.note: ⚑ Use this if you get back after 23:00, when the hotel’s free ramen has finished.

bases.title: Hiroshima — Hiroshima Station
bases.note: All of these are inside the station buildings, 3–5 minutes on foot from the hotel. They all close between 22:00 and 22:30. ⛔ After that, only convenience stores (konbini) are open. ⚠ Watch the time on Miyajima day (8 Nov): be back at Hiroshima Station by 22:00, or dinner will come from a convenience store.

options.name_jp: ユアーズ ekie広島店
options.walk: ≈375 m — ekie 1F, inside the station building
options.what: A proper supermarket inside the station, with lots of ready-to-eat food: bento, prepared dishes and local products.
options.address_jp: 〒732-0822 広島県広島市南区松原町1-2 ekie 1F
options.note: 🔴 The supermarket to use on both Hiroshima nights. ⚑ Your hotel here, the Sotetsu Fresa, is the only one of your three hotels whose website lists a microwave, so you can heat a supermarket meal. Yours closes at 22:00, so its biggest discounts start at about 20:00–21:00. The pin marks ekie; the shop is on its ground floor.

options.name_en: ekie KITCHEN — bento and deli counters
options.name_jp: ekie 1F ekie KITCHEN
options.hours: Each counter has its own hours. Expect all of them closed by 22:00, when Yours supermarket on the same floor closes.
options.walk: ≈375 m — ekie 1F, same floor as Yours
options.what: A row of takeaway counters next to Yours supermarket: Kuroben, NUMBER 8, Green gourmet and others, selling boxed meals and prepared dishes.
options.note: ⚠ The counters’ hours are not published, and some close before 22:00. Do not rely on them late in the evening.

options.name_jp: 吉野家 広島駅北口店
options.what: Beef bowls, with table seating or takeaway. Of all the hot food in the station, this closes last.
options.address_jp: 〒732-0822 広島県広島市南区松原町1-2 ekie 1F
options.note: ⚑ Closing at 22:30, this is the last hot meal near the hotel. The pin marks ekie; the shop is on its ground floor.

options.name_jp: 吉野家 ミナモア広島店
options.walk: ≈280 m — minamoa, the closest of the station buildings to the hotel
options.what: Same Yoshinoya menu as the ekie branch, with takeaway and ordering ahead from your phone. It is the nearer of the two Yoshinoya branches to the hotel.
options.address_jp: 〒732-0822 広島県広島市南区松原町2-37 ミナモア広島
options.note: ⚠ Last order is 21:30, and it closes at 22:00, half an hour before the ekie Yoshinoya. It is closer to the hotel, but it closes first.

bases.title: Day hubs — buying a lunch to carry
bases.note: 🔴 Buy food at a station you pass through. The places you are going have little or nothing. The days are in trip order.

options.name_jp: セブン-イレブン 京王高尾楓kaede店
options.kind: konbini, straight out of the ticket gate
options.hours: ⚠ Weekdays 09:00–17:00 · weekends and holidays 08:00–18:00 (April–November). 26 Oct is a Monday, so it opens at 09:00.
options.what: Onigiri, sandwiches, drinks, grilled dango and a mont-bell corner. If you get there before it opens, two 24-hour konbini are 4–5 minutes away: 7-Eleven Takaosan Inter and FamilyMart Hachiōji Takao-chō.
options.address_jp: 東京都八王子市高尾町
options.note: 🔴 Use this shop only as a backup. The day 5 plan is to buy lunch in Akihabara before you board, because an early start gets you here before this shop opens at 09:00.

options.name_en: Day 6 · Kita-Kamakura — Lawson Three-F, and NewDays at Kamakura for the way back
options.name_jp: ローソン・スリーエフ 北鎌倉店 / NewDays 鎌倉
options.kind: konbini — ⛔ nothing inside Kita-Kamakura station itself
options.hours: Lawson Three-F 24 hours · NewDays Kamakura 06:30–23:00 daily
options.walk: Lawson ≈1 minute from the Kita-Kamakura gate · NewDays is at the end of the walk, outside the gates in CIAL Kamakura 1F
options.what: Kita-Kamakura station has no shop, but a 24-hour Lawson is 1 minute outside. At the end of the walk, NewDays at Kamakura station is the last place to buy food before the train back to Tokyo.
options.address_jp: 神奈川県鎌倉市山ノ内513（ローソン）
options.note: ⚠ The Lawson is probably open 24 hours, but this is not confirmed.

options.name_en: Days 8–10 · Kintetsu Nara — FamilyMart inside the gates
options.name_jp: ファミリーマート 近鉄奈良駅改札内店
options.walk: On the concourse — you pass it without leaving the gates
options.what: Onigiri, sandwiches, bento and drinks. It is the last easy place to buy food before the Nara temples, and it opens at 05:45, earlier than any train you will take.
options.address_jp: 奈良県奈良市東向中町29
options.note: ⚑ It is inside the ticket gates, so it costs no detour on any of the three Nara days. There is no map pin: it is a shop on the station concourse, and a pin would only show the station building.

options.name_en: Day 11 · Demachiyanagi — Sizuya inside the station
options.name_jp: 志津屋 出町柳店
options.kind: bakery, inside the Eizan Railway station
options.walk: Inside the Eizan Demachiyanagi concourse, where you change trains anyway
options.what: Sizuya is a Kyoto bakery chain. Filled rolls and sandwiches are the easiest food to carry over the Kurama ridge. If you want onigiri instead, a 24-hour 7-Eleven is 1 minute outside the station.
options.address_jp: 京都市左京区田中上柳町
options.note: 🔴 Demachiyanagi station is the only place to buy food on the day 11 route. Kurama village has only souvenir stands and teahouses, and Kibuneguchi has nothing. Buy everything you want for the ridge here, when you change trains. The pin marks Sizuya inside the station; the 7-Eleven is 1 minute further out.

options.name_jp: アル・プラザ醍醐
options.hours: Ground floor 09:30–20:30 · upper floors and most specialty shops to 20:00
options.what: A full Heiwadō supermarket with the usual prepared-food and bento counters, on top of the subway station you arrive at.
options.address_jp: 京都府京都市伏見区醍醐高畑町1-37
options.note: 🔴 Opens at 09:30, after you pass it at about 08:45 on the way to Sanbō-in, so buy lunch at Kyoto Station before you leave (Kyoto Porta’s food shops open at 07:30). If you forgot: walk back here after the treasure house, about 10 min, and eat before the 13:29 train. There is no food at the temple or on the climb to Kami-Daigo.

options.name_en: Day 15 · Yoshino — nothing at the station
options.name_jp: 吉野駅
options.walk: Nearest konbini ≈2 km, at Kamiichi across the river, too far to walk between trains
options.what: ⛔ No shop or kiosk is listed for Kintetsu’s Yoshino station. The two nearest konbini are 24-hour Lawsons at Kamiichi and Riverside, too far to walk to between trains.
options.note: 🔴 Buy anything you want to carry up the Yoshino ridge in Kyoto, before you leave. ⚠ Do not count on finding a shop at Yoshino station.

options.name_en: Day 16 · Uji — no station shop; the Byōdō-in approach instead
options.name_jp: 宇治駅 / 平等院表参道
options.kind: ⛔ nothing in the station — food is on the street outside
options.hours: Station: coin lockers and a ticket window (08:00–20:00), no shop. The shops on the approach street open roughly 10:00–17:00.
options.walk: The approach runs from the station to Byōdō-in, a few minutes on the walk you are doing anyway
options.what: The JR station at Uji has no kiosk or convenience store. Right outside it, the Byōdō-in approach street (平等院表参道) has tea houses, cafés and takeaway sweets. Tea soba (soba made with green tea) is the local dish. The shops there open only in the daytime.
options.note: 🔴 The day plan has a sit-down lunch on this street after Ujigami-jinja, from about 12:30, or later if your Phoenix Hall time is late. If you want food in your bag as well, buy it at Kyoto Station before the Nara-line train.

options.name_en: Day 18 · Miyajimaguchi — 7-Eleven in the ferry terminal
options.name_jp: セブン-イレブン おみやげ街道 宮島口ターミナル店
options.kind: konbini and souvenir shop combined, in the ferry terminal
options.walk: ≈1 minute from the JR station, inside the terminal you board from
options.what: Onigiri, bread, drinks and Seven Café coffee, next to Hiroshima souvenirs. It is the last shop before the ferry.
options.address_jp: 広島県廿日市市宮島口1丁目
options.note: 🔴 Lunch on day 18 is not until 15:00–16:15, after you come down Misen. That is a long time after breakfast, with a 535 m climb in between, so buy something here to eat on the way up. The pin marks the shop itself, next to the station.

balanced.intro: Set meals with fish or meat, vegetables and rice. First, the branches near each hotel and in the city areas you visit. At the end, what to order at any other branch of each chain.
order_rules: If there’s a tablet on the table, order on it; if it has a language button, switch it to English.
If there is no tablet but there is a call button, press it and show the staff the Japanese order line from that chain’s entry.
🔴 Never point at a menu picture with カキ or 牡蠣 in its name — that means oyster. Several chains are selling oyster fry (fried oysters) this autumn.
Office lunch hour is 12:00–13:00, and the set-meal chains fill up then. Go either side of it.

ootoya.order: The everyday set (mainichi teishoku): a tray of small dishes with meat, fish, egg and vegetables. ¥1,480.
ootoya.order_jp: 毎日定食を ひとつ お願いします
ootoya.order_romaji: Mainichi teishoku o hitotsu onegai shimasu
ootoya.alt_jp: しまほっけの炭火焼きを お願いします

yayoiken.order: Salt-grilled mackerel set (¥990), plus a side salad (¥100).

yayoiken.order_romaji: Saba no shioyaki teishoku to yasai sarada o onegai shimasu
yayoiken.alt_jp: しまほっけ定食を お願いします
notes: Rice refills are free. You can switch to barley rice (もち麦ごはん); after that, only white rice is refilled.
If there’s a ticket machine by the door, buy a ticket first. The button reads サバの塩焼定食 (salt-grilled mackerel set).

jonathan.alt: For more vegetables, add Jonathan’s salad.
jonathan.alt_jp: ジョナサンサラダを お願いします

royalhost.order_jp: 気仙沼産メカジキのしょうが焼き膳を お願いします
royalhost.order_romaji: Kesennuma-san mekajiki no shōgayaki zen o onegai shimasu
royalhost.alt_jp: グリルサーモンサラダを お願いします
notes: 🔴 The menu has two versions of this set. The ¥2,508 one comes with 牡蠣フライ — oyster fry. Point at the ¥2,013 one.

dish_guides.intro: What to do at the table, by dish — not by restaurant. Every line is true of the dish wherever it is served, and anything that depends on what the shop puts in front of you is written as a condition, so nothing here tells you a table has something on it that it may not.

steps.text: First mouthful with nothing on it — a few strands straight off the pile.
Lift a few strands at a time and dip them. Don’t tip the broth over the noodles: a small dip at a time is what keeps the broth hot, and cold broth wrecks the bowl.
When the noodles are gone, ask for sūpu-wari (スープ割り) — the broth comes back thinned with hot dashi, to drink. Some counters put a pot out to do it yourself, and some shops don’t offer it at all.
Pour the hot dashi in a little at a time and taste as you go. All at once and it goes flat.

If a small mortar of sesame seeds is on the table, grind it while you wait. Stop when you can smell the sesame — about seven-tenths ground — then pour the sauce into the mortar and dip the cutlet in that. Plenty of shops don’t do sesame at all.
Start two or three slices in from the wide, meaty end rather than at the near edge — that is where the frying lands most evenly.
Eat the first pieces bare — or with salt, if salt is on the table — and leave any sauce for the last two or three. Sauce on a hot cutlet softens the crust immediately.

guides.title: Sukiyaki — beef in the iron pan

steps.text: If the egg comes whole, beat it in the small bowl before the first meat is ready. That bowl is the one thing at this table that is yours to do.
If a server is cooking the pot, leave it alone: don’t turn the meat, don’t add anything, take what is put in front of you.
Roll the meat through the egg and eat it straight away. The egg drops the temperature enough to eat it hot off the pan, and takes the edge off the sugar-and-soy.
Look at what arrives. Noodles already sitting in hot broth: there is nothing to dip and no ritual — eat. Noodles on a basket or tray with the broth in a separate cup: dip.
Hot bowl: a light shake of shichimi if the shaker is there. The broth in a hot bowl is mixed weaker than dipping broth, so drinking it down is normal.
Take a small amount per mouthful and pull air in with the noodles. The slurp is the point, not a lapse.
Eat it inside about five minutes. Soba goes soft fast.
Cold tray only: dip the last third of the noodles, not the whole length. Wasabi goes on the noodles, not stirred into the broth.
Cold tray only: soba-yu, the cloudy cooking water, may come at the end — pour it into the leftover dipping broth and drink that. It isn’t served everywhere, and a hot bowl usually doesn’t get it.
If it is set down on the hot plate in front of you, eat it there with the small spatula (hera) — or ask for chopsticks if you would rather. On a dish, chopsticks.
Cut bite-sized squares off the near edge as you go — not pizza wedges. A wedge will not sit on the hera.
Work through the cabbage side before you get into the noodle layer. The noodles hold the heat and will burn your mouth.

guides.title: Kamameshi — rice in its own iron pot

steps.text: Lift the lid and mix the toppings right through the rice before serving any of it. The rice against the hot iron comes out firmer than the rice in the middle, and mixing is what evens that out.
The pot slides while you stir and the iron is hot — steady it with the towel or a napkin rather than a bare hand.
Serve one bowl at a time and put the lid back on between them, or what is left dries out.
The scorched layer on the bottom is the last thing out of the pot. If it won’t lift, put the lid back for a minute — under-steamed okoge is what refuses to come away.
If there is hot tea or dashi at the table, the last bowlful takes it poured over.

guides.title: Anago-meshi — grilled conger eel on rice

steps.text: Eaten in, it comes hot off the grill — nothing to add, nothing to mix.

The box is not a bowl that went cold: it is built to be eaten at room temperature, and it keeps improving for the first couple of hours as the tare works down into the rice. Don’t go looking for somewhere to reheat it.

guides.title: Kakinoha-zushi — sushi in a persimmon leaf

steps.text: Peel the leaf back from one side only, like a banana skin, until half the sushi shows, and eat it straight out of the leaf. Your fingers never touch the rice.
The leaf is not eaten. It is there to keep the fish, and it is bitter.
Room temperature is the point — the rice is at its best around 20°C. If a box has been sitting somewhere cold, give it time out of the bag before you start.

guides.title: Grilled fish — saikyō-yaki and any yakizakana

steps.text: Work from the left across to the right, taking the upper, backbone side before the belly. On a fillet that means straight along from the near edge rather than digging into the middle.
Never turn the fish over. If it is a whole fish, lift the backbone clear with the chopsticks and eat the underside where it lies.
Put the bones together at the far side of the plate as they come out.
Eat the skin with the flesh rather than leaving it at the side.

mendokoro-honda.order_backup: Richer: tokusei shōyu ramen (特製醤油ラーメン) — the same bowl with 7 slices of pork, a marinated soft-boiled egg and better nori. Shio tsukemen (塩つけ麺), cold noodles in kombu water with seaweed salt and sudachi lime, is the shop's other famous order, but it is a summer dish.

kamayoshi.order_how: 🔴 Ticket machine just inside the door. Buy your ticket first, then sit down and hand it to the staff. The shop is listed as taking cards, Suica and QR, but the machine may not take them, so carry cash. 14 seats, no reservations. ⚠ The shop asks for two things in writing. It has no space for luggage, so don't arrive with the trolley: leave it at the hotel first. At weekday lunch, give up the table 20–30 min after eating. Neither rule affects you at dinner.

Labels: ごぼう天うどん (tokyo-tabearuki); とりちくわ天うどん, 肉うどん, あつあつ/ひやひや (tablemark.co.jp/udon/tkubiyori/86.html). The old card said "no ticket machine" — contradicted by all three. Read 2026-09-21.
kamayoshi.order: Gobō-ten udon (ごぼう天うどん): udon topped with big pieces of burdock root, fried fresh in tempura batter.
kamayoshi.order_jp: ごぼう天うどんを ひとつ お願いします
kamayoshi.order_romaji: Gobō-ten udon o hitotsu onegai shimasu
kamayoshi.order_why: The owner is from Fukuoka, so the broth is Hakata-style: flying fish with kombu and katsuo (bonito). The noodles are Sanuki-style: thick and firm to bite, made in-house from Kagawa wheat. Burdock tempura is one of the two classic toppings on Hakata udon, so this bowl shows off the Fukuoka side of the shop.
kamayoshi.order_backup: The shop's reported best-seller: tori-chikuwa-ten udon (とりちくわ天うどん), chicken and fish-cake (chikuwa) tempura, fried after you order. Beef: niku udon (肉うどん). Every bowl comes hot or cold. Three Special sets combine several tempura: A has 4 kinds (chicken, chikuwa, aubergine, maitake mushroom); B has 3 kinds, plus beef and a hot-spring egg; C has 5 kinds, plus beef.

tonkatsu-marugo.order_how: 🔴 Cash only: no cards, no IC, no QR. Bring notes. Table service, no reservations. ⚑ The long queue here is at lunch: about 29 people waiting for the 11:30 opening, against 2 people at 16:50 for the 17:00 dinner opening. Arrive at the 17:00 opening and expect to wait about 10 min; arrive later and it can be about 40 min. Your order includes the set (定食, teishoku): a few hundred yen more for rice, pickles and red-miso soup, with free refills of rice and cabbage.
tonkatsu-marugo.order: Toku-rōsu katsu teishoku (特ロースかつ定食): the premium pork loin cutlet, thick-cut with its fat edge left on, as a set meal.
tonkatsu-marugo.order_jp: 特ロースかつ定食を ひとつ お願いします
tonkatsu-marugo.order_romaji: Toku-rōsu katsu teishoku o hitotsu onegai shimasu
tonkatsu-marugo.order_en: One premium pork loin cutlet set meal, please.
tonkatsu-marugo.order_why: Marugo has fried tonkatsu since 1975, using Yamagata sangen-ton pork. Its two best-known cutlets are the premium loin and the premium fillet. The loin is the fattier of the two and the one people talk about most. The shop is on the 2026 Tonkatsu Hyakumeiten list (“100 famous tonkatsu shops”).
tonkatsu-marugo.order_backup: Leaner: toku-hire katsu (特ヒレかつ), the premium fillet cutlet, cooked the same way. It has no fat edge and costs a little more. Order it if you would rather not eat pork fat after a long day.

ponta-honke.order_how: Table service on three floors: a 3-seat counter on the ground floor, more seats upstairs. Cards accepted. ⚠ Reservations are for 2 or more only, so on your own you walk in: go early. Closed Mondays.
ponta-honke.order: Katsuretsu (カツレツ), a pork cutlet: the centre of the loin with all the fat trimmed off, fried slowly in lard the kitchen renders itself.
ponta-honke.order_jp: カツレツを ひとつ お願いします
ponta-honke.order_why: Ponta opened in 1905. Its founder had cooked Western food in the Imperial Household kitchen. Its katsuretsu is an early form of the cutlet that later became tonkatsu across Japan. The cutlet cooks for over ten minutes in low-temperature lard, then briefly in hot lard, and comes without a heavy sauce. The result is closer to a French côtelette than to modern tonkatsu. The cutlet is the reason to come here.
ponta-honke.order_backup: Stews: tongue stew, tan-shichū (タンシチュー), which the shop recommends, and beef stew. ⚠ Both cost nearly twice as much as the cutlet.

delhi-ueno.order_how: 🔴 Cash only: no cards, no e-money. 15 seats at a counter and small tables. No reservations. Open 11:50–21:30 with no afternoon break, so any hour works.
delhi-ueno.order: Kashmir curry (カシミールカレー): a jet-black, very thin, very hot curry poured over rice.
delhi-ueno.order_jp: カシミールカレーを ひとつ お願いします
delhi-ueno.order_romaji: Kashmīru karē o hitotsu onegai shimasu
delhi-ueno.order_why: Delhi has been on this corner since 1956, and Kashmir curry is what it is famous for. The menu rates it 5 chillies out of 5, the hottest on the menu. It is thin enough to drink and much hotter than it looks. The heat is the point of the dish.
delhi-ueno.order_backup: Want less heat? Order a milder curry by name. Delhi curry (デリーカレー): mild, 1 chilli out of 5. Indo curry (インドカレー): 3 chillies, thicker and more like an ordinary curry.

gonokami-seisakusho.order_how: 🔴 Ticket machine, inside the shop. 🔴 Cash only. If nobody is waiting outside, walk in and buy a ticket. If people are queuing on the street, join the end and wait for staff to call you in. Do not walk past the queue to the machine. ⚑ At the time you will arrive there is usually no queue. ⚑ When you hand over the ticket, staff ask one question: nami-mori or ko-mori (並盛 / 小盛), regular or small portion? Say 'nami-mori' for regular.
