gonokami-seisakusho.order_jp: 海老つけ麺を ひとつ お願いします
gonokami-seisakusho.order_romaji: Ebi tsukemen o hitotsu onegai shimasu
gonokami-seisakusho.order_why: The shop is built around prawn tsukemen, and this is the basic bowl that the other versions start from. Under the shrimp is a stock of pork and chicken bones with mackerel and dried sardine. The shrimp thickens the soup, so it clings to the noodles.
gonokami-seisakusho.order_backup: Ebi tomato tsukemen (海老トマトつけ麺): the same soup with a sharper taste. It is the one regulars switch to. Ebi miso tsukemen (海老味噌つけ麺): the same soup, heavier. If you want a topping, add a marinated egg (味玉).

fish-shinjuku.order_how: Table service, 29 seats, walk-in only. It takes no online reservations, and it takes bookings by phone only. Evening walk-ins are usually seated. Cards, Suica and QR accepted. ⚠ Closed 15:00–17:00: come for lunch or in the evening.
fish-shinjuku.order: Three-curry combo (3種コンボ): keema and a mixed-bean curry are fixed, and you choose the third. Chicken is the plain choice. All three come on one plate with rice, pickles and side dishes.
fish-shinjuku.order_jp: 3種コンボを ひとつ、カレーは チキンで お願いします
fish-shinjuku.order_romaji: Sanshu konbo o hitotsu, karē wa chikin de onegai shimasu
fish-shinjuku.order_en: One three-curry combo, please, with chicken as the curry.
fish-shinjuku.order_why: The combo plate is the house format. FISH carries on a curry shop that served this plate in Ark Hills, Roppongi, for about 30 years. The name, the recipes and the Indian head chef all moved here when it reopened. The three curries are meant to be eaten together with the sides. The spicing is distinctive but not too hot.
fish-shinjuku.order_backup: Choices for the third curry: chicken, extra-hot chicken, white fish, prawn, pork, or the curry of the week. The two-curry combo (2種コンボ) is a smaller version. On the Mt Takao day, lunch is onigiri on the mountain, so you will probably want the full three-curry combo.

kawashige-kamakura.order_how: Table service, 40 seats (8 at the counter), walk-in. 🔴 Cash only. Shirasu comes two ways: nama (生, raw) and kama-age (釜揚げ, boiled). Raw depends on that morning's catch, so it is not always on; boiled always is.
kawashige-kamakura.order: Shirasu-don (しらす丼): Sagami Bay whitebait heaped over rice — Kamakura's signature dish.
kawashige-kamakura.order_jp: しらす丼を ひとつ お願いします
kawashige-kamakura.order_why: Raw shirasu bowls are a recognised Kanagawa regional dish, and Kawashige buys its whitebait from Sagami Bay. The season runs 11 March to 31 December and peaks twice; the autumn fish are the fatter. Raw shirasu can only be served on the day it is landed.
kawashige-kamakura.order_backup: Tempura bowls are the house speciality: large-prawn tendon (大海老天丼, ¥2,100) and house tendon (川茂天丼, ¥3,500), finished with a sauce handed down from the sister house founded in 1887. Also an eel bowl (うな丼) and a seafood bowl (海鮮丼).

honke-daiichi-asahi.order_how: Staff take your order at the table; there is no ticket machine. Cards and QR accepted. 31 seats, no reservations. Expect a queue outside at almost any hour: it is open from 06:00 until 01:00. ⚠ Closed Thursdays.
honke-daiichi-asahi.order: Ramen (ラーメン): thin straight noodles in a pork-and-soy broth, topped with sliced chāshū (roast pork), a heap of Kujō leek (Kyoto green onion) and mung-bean sprouts.
honke-daiichi-asahi.order_jp: ラーメンを ひとつ お願いします
honke-daiichi-asahi.order_why: The original Kyoto-style ramen. The shop has stood at the Takabashi corner since 1947, and the other shops called Daiichi-Asahi grew out of it. The broth looks heavy but tastes light. The pork is the main attraction.
honke-daiichi-asahi.order_backup: Tokusei rāmen (特製ラーメン) is the large size: about double the whole bowl, noodles included, with about 5 slices of chāshū instead of the usual few. For extra pork without extra noodles, order chāshū-men (チャーシューメン). ⚠ Both are a lot of pork for a late dinner: order one only if you skipped lunch.

kaidashimen-kitada.order_how: 🔴 Ticket machine just inside the door, on your right: buy a ticket first, then sit down. It is a display-type machine and takes cashless payment. 11 seats, no reservations. ⚑ Open 07:00–22:00 with no midday break, so it is serving at almost any hour you get back to Kyoto.

machine_buttons.en: Side: shellfish simmered in soy, over rice

kaidashimen-kitada.machine_src: kyotopi.jp/articles/rnb0L (article 2024-09-04): 「店内入ってすぐ右手に券売機」, display-type, cashless; labels 貝だし麺 / 蛤らぁ麺 / 中華そば / 貝のしぐれ煮ごはん. Read 2026-09-21. The old card said "Order at the counter".
kaidashimen-kitada.order: Kai-dashi men: ramen in a clear broth simmered from asari clams, hamaguri clams and scallops. ⚑ It is not meat-free: the ramen comes topped with chāshū (pork), and pork and chicken both appear on the menu.
kaidashimen-kitada.order_jp: 貝だし麺を ひとつ お願いします
kaidashimen-kitada.order_romaji: Kai-dashi men o hitotsu onegai shimasu
kaidashimen-kitada.order_why: The shop is built around this one bowl, and it is why the shop is on Tabelog's Ramen WEST Hyakumeiten list for 2025 (100 famous ramen shops, west Japan). Shellfish broth is much lighter than pork broth. That is how the shop can serve from 07:00 to 22:00 without a break.
kaidashimen-kitada.order_backup: Hamaguri rā-men (蛤らぁ麺): the shop's other main bowl, made with hamaguri clams only. Add a small bowl of shellfish simmered in soy over rice (貝のしぐれ煮ご飯, from ¥200) if the ramen alone is not enough for dinner.

yamamoto-mambo.order_how: 🔴 Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR. Food is cooked on the griddle in front of you and eaten off it. About half of the 23 seats are at the griddle. Reservations are accepted on weekdays only, with none at weekends or on holidays. All three visits here are on weekdays.
yamamoto-mambo.order: Manbo-yaki, the house dish: a thin beta-yaki pancake with noodles folded in, built in layers. It is quite different from Osaka or Hiroshima okonomiyaki. ⚑ The plain one has one filling, which you choose when you order: meat, squid, or abura-kasu (crisp rendered offal). The Special (スペシャル) has all three, plus egg and spring onion.
yamamoto-mambo.order_jp: まんぼ焼きを ひとつ お願いします
yamamoto-mambo.order_why: The shop opened in 1948 and is known for manbo-yaki, its own development of beta-yaki. Beta-yaki is Kyoto's own kind of okonomiyaki, little known outside the city. There are two stories about the name: a customer groaning "manbo" at the taste, or the shape of the manbō (sunfish). If you order plain beta-yaki here, you miss the dish the shop is known for.
yamamoto-mambo.order_backup: Beta-yaki (ベタ焼き): the same base without the noodles. Lighter, and a better choice if you had a big lunch.

arata.order_how: 🔴 Cash only: no cards, no e-money, no QR payment. Griddle (teppan) restaurant with 50 seats. ⚠ Evenings only, from 17:00. Closed Sundays.
arata.order: Arata okonomi, the house okonomiyaki, made in the manbo-yaki style: built up in layers. A thin batter base, cabbage and konjac, spring onion, fish powder, and agi (beef jaw meat), which gives it its chew. ⚑ It comes in two versions about ¥300 apart, with noodles and without, under two different names. This description is of the noodle version: if you want noodles, say “soba” when you order.
arata.order_jp: あらたお好みを ひとつ お願いします
arata.order_romaji: Arata okonomi o hitotsu onegai shimasu
arata.order_why: Agi (beef jaw meat) makes this different from every other okonomiyaki on the trip. Most places don't use the cut, because it takes a long time to cook. As it cooks, its fat makes the whole pancake savoury. The shop has been listed in the Tabelog Hyakumeiten (the top 100 okonomiyaki places) several times because of it.
arata.order_backup: Milder: plain beta-yaki (ベタ焼き), without the agi. If you would rather not have a pancake, order a griddle dish instead: agi grilled with salt (あぎ塩焼き), or tetchan-yaki (てっちゃん焼き, grilled beef offal).

moritaya-kyoto-isetan.order_how: Sukiyaki restaurant with table service on the 11th floor of the Isetan department store above Kyoto Station, with a view over the city to the eastern hills. 🔴 Cash or card only: no IC cards (Suica, ICOCA) and no QR payment. There is a queue for the floor 18:00–19:00; after 19:00 you can usually walk in. Last entry and last order 21:00. ⚠ Lunch prices end at 16:00.
moritaya-kyoto-isetan.order: Sukiyaki (すき焼き): kuroge wagyū (Japanese black beef) cooked at the table in an iron pan with sugar and soy, then dipped in raw beaten egg.
moritaya-kyoto-isetan.order_jp: すき焼きを ひとつ お願いします
moritaya-kyoto-isetan.order_why: Morita-ya opened in 1869 as Kyoto's first beef shop. Since 1981 it has raised its own cattle on a farm at Wachi in Funai, north-west of Kyoto, so the beef on your plate comes from its own herd. The sukiyaki set comes in courses: a starter, then the beef with vegetables and egg, then rice, red-miso soup, pickles and a dessert.
moritaya-kyoto-isetan.order_backup: Shabu-shabu: the same beef swished through hot stock instead of simmered in sugar and soy. It is lighter and less sweet than sukiyaki; order it if sukiyaki sounds too heavy after a long day. Also on the menu: oil-yaki (オイル焼き), the same beef seared on an iron plate, and a separate steak course.

wakakusa-curry.order_how: Order at the table. Cards, Suica and QR accepted. 26 seats, no reservations. ⚑ Aigake (あいがけ) is a menu item: choose two of the four curries (Wakakusa, mild, brown, chicken) and get them side by side on one plate.
wakakusa-curry.order: Wakakusa curry (若草カレー), the house curry: spinach, tomato and other vegetables with chicken, strongly spiced. Only the vegetables and spices thicken it; there is no flour roux.
wakakusa-curry.order_jp: 若草カレーを ひとつ お願いします
wakakusa-curry.order_romaji: Wakakusa karē o hitotsu onegai shimasu
wakakusa-curry.order_why: The shop is named after this curry, and it earned the shop its place on the Curry WEST Hyakumeiten list ("100 famous curry shops, west Japan"). It is dense and strongly spiced, with little sweetness. Most Japanese curry is thickened with a flour roux; the shop says nothing thickens this one except the vegetables and spices. The shop is in a covered shopping street about 5 min on foot from Kintetsu Nara station.
wakakusa-curry.order_backup: Chicken curry: creamy with coconut milk, and mild. Mildest: Yamato-beef mild curry (大和牛マイルドカレー), a sweet roux curry the shop says a small child can eat. A good choice after a long day. Hottest: lamb brown curry (ラムブラウンカレー), slow-simmered lamb. ⚑ Can't choose? Order aigake: two curries on one plate.

kamameshi-shizuka-koen.order_how: Table and tatami seating, 43 seats, no reservations. Cards and QR accepted. 🔴 Each pot is cooked from raw after you order, one at a time over a direct flame. Expect about 20 min before it reaches the table, so this is a slow lunch. The long cooking is what gives the rice its crisp, scorched crust at the bottom. ⚠ The times the shop publishes are last-order times; the shop closes later. Queues: about 30 min in the first hour of service on a weekday, longer at weekends, gone by mid-afternoon. Mid-afternoon is the best time to come today.
kamameshi-shizuka-koen.order: Nara nanashu kamameshi (奈良七種釜めし): rice cooked to order in its own iron pot, under many toppings, including prawn, crab, conger eel, chicken, burdock, carrot, shiitake and bamboo shoot.
kamameshi-shizuka-koen.order_jp: 奈良七種釜めしを ひとつ お願いします
kamameshi-shizuka-koen.order_romaji: Nara nanashu kamameshi o hitotsu onegai shimasu
kamameshi-shizuka-koen.order_en: One Nara nanashu kamameshi (rice pot with mixed toppings), please.
kamameshi-shizuka-koen.order_why: The shop's most popular pot. The house has cooked kamameshi in Nara for more than 60 years, and this branch is directly opposite the Nara National Museum. The nanashu (七種) in the name means a wide mix of toppings, with no fixed number. Scrape the bottom of the pot: the scorched rice there, okoge, is the part people come back for.
kamameshi-shizuka-koen.order_backup: Lighter and cheaper: single-ingredient pots, cooked in the same time. Choose young chicken, prawn, crab, or shimeji mushrooms with mountain vegetables. ⚑ Autumn special: a matsutake pot, a limited number each day, not on the regular price list. Matsutake season is roughly September to October, and the 31st is the very end of it, so it may not be on. Ask; don't plan on it.

icchan-honten.order_how: 🔴 Cash only: no cards, IC or QR. A small room with counter, griddle-side and table seats. No reservations: walk in. ⚑ Staff ask one question when you order: soba, udon or no noodles in the pancake. Say soba, the Hiroshima standard.
icchan-honten.order: Niku-tama soba (肉玉そば), the standard Hiroshima okonomiyaki: a thin crêpe, a large heap of cabbage, pork belly, fried noodles and an egg, pressed together on the griddle.
icchan-honten.order_jp: 肉玉そばを ひとつ お願いします
icchan-honten.order_romaji: Niku-tama soba o hitotsu onegai shimasu
icchan-honten.order_en: One niku-tama soba (pork-and-egg okonomiyaki with soba noodles), please.
icchan-honten.order_why: Hiroshima okonomiyaki is built in layers. In Osaka the ingredients are mixed together. Niku-tama soba is the basic version that every Hiroshima shop is judged on. Icchan was in Tabelog's Okonomiyaki Hyakumeiten (top 100 list) in 2019, 2024 and 2025. Its banner says it has been in the Michelin guide six years running. The guides it names are Hiroshima 2013 and Hiroshima–Ehime 2018, so its latest Bib Gourmand is from 2018. The owner is the second generation. He took over his father's shop and runs it under his own name.
icchan-honten.order_backup: Toppings are listed on the left side of the menu, most ¥300–350: spring onion, squid tempura (イカ天), prawn, cheese, squid, garlic, mochi. Squid tempura is the local favourite. Ask for udon instead of soba if you want it softer, or for no noodles at all.

okonomiyaki-masaru.order_how: Okonomiyaki and teppanyaki counter. 20 seats, all round the iron griddle, and no tables, so you eat where the food is cooked. No cards; QR payment accepted. Reservations are by phone only, so plan to walk in. Lunch 11:30–14:00 (last order 13:30), dinner 17:30–23:00 (last order 22:00).
okonomiyaki-masaru.order: Niku-tama soba (肉玉そば): the layered Hiroshima okonomiyaki with pork, egg and noodles, finished in front of you.
okonomiyaki-masaru.order_jp: 肉玉そばを ひとつ お願いします
okonomiyaki-masaru.order_romaji: Niku-tama soba o hitotsu onegai shimasu
okonomiyaki-masaru.order_en: One niku-tama soba (pork-and-egg okonomiyaki with soba noodles), please.
okonomiyaki-masaru.order_why: Niku-tama soba is the basic version of the Hiroshima style, so it is a fair comparison with the other okonomiyaki on the trip. Masaru is also a teppanyaki counter and costs more than a plain okonomiyaki shop. The griddle dishes are a real part of what you pay for.
okonomiyaki-masaru.order_backup: Order a teppanyaki dish as well as the okonomiyaki. There are about 20 of them, and they are why Masaru costs more than the shops near it. ⚠ Don't expect a printed list of toppings: ask at the counter. Look for squid tempura (イカ天), the local favourite all over Hiroshima.

kunimatsu-ekie.order_how: 🔴 Ticket machine: buy your ticket before you sit down. ⚠ No credit cards, but Suica and nanaco are accepted. Counter seats only, no reservations. It is inside ekie at Hiroshima Station, so you don't need to go outside.
kunimatsu-ekie.machine_hint: Older reviews print the set as ごまハーフ＆ハーフセット.
kunimatsu-ekie.machine_src: Machine at the entrance: tabicocolo.com and syokuki.com snippets. Label: syokuki.com/archives/21295 (2018 — old; the 2026 machine may differ). Read 2026-09-21. Machine layout NOT seen.
kunimatsu-ekie.order: Half-and-half (ハーフ＆ハーフ): one bowl with each shop's shiru-nashi tantanmen (Hiroshima's soupless dandan noodles) side by side, with a soft-boiled egg and rice.
kunimatsu-ekie.order_jp: ハーフ＆ハーフを ひとつ お願いします
kunimatsu-ekie.order_romaji: Hāfu ando hāfu o hitotsu onegai shimasu
kunimatsu-ekie.order_why: This counter is run jointly by two of Hiroshima's best-known soupless tantanmen shops, Kunimatsu and Musashibō. The half-and-half lets you eat both shops' noodles side by side. Kunimatsu makes only a sesame version. Musashibō makes sesame or soy, but both halves may come sesame. If you order a single bowl, you miss the comparison this counter exists for.
kunimatsu-ekie.order_backup: Either shop's bowl on its own, if you don't want to compare. Each shop puts its own Sichuan pepper on the table, with chilli oil, extra sauce and vinegar: add them to taste. Locals stir the noodles thoroughly before the first mouthful. The set comes with rice and a soft-boiled egg. If you don't want the rice, you get a second egg instead.

yakigaki-no-hayashi.order_how: Table and tatami seating, 86 seats, about 10 min up Omotesandō from the pier. Cards and QR payment accepted; IC cards (Suica) are not. No reservations at present. 🔴 Last order 16:30, half an hour before closing. 🔴 The shop has two menu cards, and the anago is on the second. The first card is the oyster menu (牡蠣お品書き). The one you want is the other menu (その他お品書き): ask for it if only the oyster card arrives.
yakigaki-no-hayashi.order: Anago-meshi (あなご飯（汁付）), ¥2,900: conger eel grilled in the shop’s own sauce, on rice, with soup.
yakigaki-no-hayashi.order_jp: あなご飯を ひとつ お願いします
yakigaki-no-hayashi.order_en: One anago-meshi (conger eel on rice), please.
yakigaki-no-hayashi.order_why: Anago-meshi is Miyajima’s other famous dish, after oysters, and Hayashi is the big restaurant on Omotesandō that serves it. The better-known anago restaurants in the area are much smaller, 16 and 32 seats (Ueno, the backup, has 32), so whether you get in depends on the queue. Hayashi has 86 seats, which matters after a climb of 535 m of stone steps with a ferry to catch.
yakigaki-no-hayashi.order_backup: All from the second menu card: grilled anago without rice (あなごのかば焼, ¥2,700); anago-musubi, 2 rice balls for ¥1,200; tempura udon ¥1,200; ten-zaru soba (cold soba with tempura) ¥1,900; tonkatsu set ¥2,800; fried-prawn set ¥3,200. ⚠ Everything on the first card is oysters: do not order from it.

tonkatsu-hasegawa-ryogoku.order_how: Cards and QR accepted. No e-money (Suica). 40 seats, with a tatami room. 2 min from the east exit of Ryōgoku station, on Yokozuna Yokochō, behind a red noren (entrance curtain). ⚠ It takes bookings for dinner (never for lunch) and stops taking them once the evening is full. So walk in early in the dinner service.
tonkatsu-hasegawa-ryogoku.order: Toku-rōsu katsu teishoku (特ロースかつ定食): the premium pork loin cutlet set, made with Hirata Bokujō pork fried in fresh panko.
tonkatsu-hasegawa-ryogoku.order_jp: 特ロースかつ定食を ひとつ お願いします
tonkatsu-hasegawa-ryogoku.order_romaji: Toku-rōsu katsu teishoku o hitotsu onegai shimasu
tonkatsu-hasegawa-ryogoku.order_en: One premium pork loin cutlet set, please.
tonkatsu-hasegawa-ryogoku.order_why: The cut the shop is best known for. The pork is Bark sangen-ton from Hirata Bokujō, a single named farm. ⚑ It comes with salt and wasabi. Try a corner with salt alone before you add sauce.
tonkatsu-hasegawa-ryogoku.order_backup: The fillet cutlet (ヒレかつ) is leaner. ⚑ Chanko is Ryōgoku's local dish, and you have it at lunch today, so tonkatsu for dinner is a change from it.

kyoto-yamaroku.order_how: Order at the table. Cards and QR accepted; e-money not. 21 seats in the basement of the Isetan department store attached to Kyoto Station, so you don't need to go outside. No reservations, and there is a queue at lunchtime. ⚠ Two services, closed mid-afternoon: lunch 11:00–15:00, dinner 16:00–20:00.
kyoto-yamaroku.order: Saikyō-yaki set: fish cured in sweet white Kyoto miso and grilled, with small seasonal side dishes, rice, miso soup and pickles. Pick the sablefish (gindara).
kyoto-yamaroku.order_jp: 西京焼き定食を ひとつ お願いします
kyoto-yamaroku.order_romaji: Saikyō-yaki teishoku o hitotsu onegai shimasu
kyoto-yamaroku.order_why: The parent company has cured fish in saikyō miso for over 90 years, and this is its first restaurant, so you eat the company's own product where it is made. The miso draws water out of the fish and sweetens it, so it grills denser than plain fish. Sablefish is always on the menu (it is not a daily special), and it turns out soft where the other fish turn out firm.
kyoto-yamaroku.order_backup: You choose the fish. Also on the menu: salmon, Spanish mackerel and mackerel, plus a pork version. ⚑ The small side dishes change with the season, and they are half the reason to have the set rather than a single grilled fish.

ginjo-ramen-kubota.order_how: 🔴 Ticket machine: buy your ticket before you sit. 🔴 Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR. 10 seats, counter only, no reservations. It closes between the lunch and evening services, so it is shut in the middle of the afternoon.

machine_buttons.en: The soy ramen — the lighter bowl

ginjo-ramen-kubota.machine_hint: The order is printed with つけ麺 BEFORE 味噌, not the way it is spoken.
ginjo-ramen-kubota.machine_src: Miso tsukemen label 「吟醸つけ麺 味噌」: kyoto-gourmet.info/kyoto-ramen/miso/kubota (page dated 2026-08-17, one review — it also calls the soy bowl 鶏醤油ラーメン, which disagrees with the card's 吟醸醤油らーめん; unresolved). Machine just inside the entrance: 4travel/Hotpepper snippet, read 2026-09-21. Machine layout NOT seen.
ginjo-ramen-kubota.order: Ginjō miso tsukemen: thick noodles you dip into a broth of three misos (Shinshū miso, gochujang and tenmenjan), stir-fried in a wok with minced pork, fish powder and the shop's own chilli oil.
ginjo-ramen-kubota.order_jp: 吟醸味噌つけ麺を ひとつ お願いします
ginjo-ramen-kubota.order_romaji: Ginjō miso tsukemen o hitotsu onegai shimasu
ginjo-ramen-kubota.order_why: Miso tsukemen is unusual anywhere, and this one is on the Ramen WEST Hyakumeiten list (a top-100 ramen list). The chilli oil and fish powder make it sharper and hotter than a soy-based dipping broth. ⚑ Ginjō in the name has nothing to do with sake here. It means carefully chosen ingredients and slow brewing, and is used of miso and soy sauce as well as of drink. The shop is known for the miso tsukemen; its plain ramen is the less famous dish.
ginjo-ramen-kubota.order_backup: Ginjō shōyu rāmen (吟醸醤油らーめん): a classic soy-sauce ramen, and a lighter meal than the tsukemen.

ami-ryogoku.order_how: Cards, Suica and QR accepted. 120 seats at tables, tatami and sunken hearths. Open 11:00–24:00 without a break. It takes bookings as well as walk-ins. ⚑ The pot cooks at your table on a portable burner, so allow time. The lunch chanko sets cost much less than the evening ones.
ami-ryogoku.order: Chanko-nabe (ちゃんこ鍋): the stew sumo stables cook for their wrestlers, with chicken, seafood and vegetables, simmered at your table.
ami-ryogoku.order_jp: ちゃんこ鍋を ひとつ お願いします
ami-ryogoku.order_why: Chanko is what sumo wrestlers eat in their stables, so Ryōgoku, a few streets from the Kokugikan (the sumo hall), is the place to try it. The shop says its recipe was handed down from a sumo stable. Some listings name the Isegahama stable; the shop itself does not. The chicken version is the traditional one. A chicken stands on two legs, and a wrestler down on all fours has lost, so stables kept four-legged meat out of the pot. Stables have mostly dropped this superstition since the 1960s. Chicken chanko is still eaten mainly before tournaments and at New Year.
ami-ryogoku.order_backup: Seafood chanko is the lighter pot. ⚑ At the end, ask for rice or noodles to be cooked in the leftover broth. That is how the stables finish the pot, and by then the broth holds most of the flavour.

chanko-kirishima-edonoren.order_how: 🔴 Order a lunch set (hiru-gozen), not the lunch course. The course (昼十両, ¥3,850) is for 2 or more people: the menu says こちらのメニューは二人前よりご注文承ります ("this item is served for two or more"). The sets have no minimum: each person gets their own chanko in a paper pot. ⚠ The sets are sold on weekdays only. Today is a Tuesday, so they are available. Cards, Suica and QR accepted. 88 seats. Cooked at your table. It is inside the Edo NOREN building, right outside the west exit of Ryōgoku station. The building has a full-size sumo ring in its atrium.
chanko-kirishima-edonoren.order: Hiru-gozen (昼御膳), the weekday lunch set: chanko for one in a paper pot, made to the Michinoku stable's recipe, with small side dishes and sashimi. West set (昼御膳-西-) ¥1,650. East set (昼御膳-東-) ¥2,200, with 5 pieces of sashimi and fried chicken added.
chanko-kirishima-edonoren.order_jp: 昼御膳を ひとつ お願いします
chanko-kirishima-edonoren.order_why: The restaurant belongs to the former ōzeki (sumo's second-highest rank) Kirishima. The shop says the pot follows his own stable's recipe. The ceremonial apron he wore as a wrestler hangs in the room. The Michinoku stable no longer exists. He reached the sumo association's retirement age of 65 in April 2024, the stable closed, and its wrestlers moved to the Otowayama stable. The Edo NOREN building is worth a look in itself: it has a full-size sumo ring (dohyō) on the ground floor.
chanko-kirishima-edonoren.order_backup: Kirishima teba-saki, the shop's own fried chicken wings, ¥700. The menu lists them next to the pot. ⚑ The lunch set comes complete on a tray, so don't expect rice or noodles cooked in the leftover broth at the end. That comes with a full pot, which you get at Ami, the first-choice lunch.

hiraso-horyuji.order_how: Table service, at the Hōryū-ji gate. Part shop, part restaurant, with a café counter. You can eat in or buy boxes to take away in the same building.
hiraso-horyuji.order: Nara lunch (奈良ランチ): four kinds of kakinoha-zushi (sushi wrapped in a persimmon leaf), a bowl of Miwa sōmen, a seasonal dish, pickles and a dessert. From October to June the sōmen comes hot, as nyūmen. ⚑ Ask for the Nara lunch by name; the plainer trays are different sets.
hiraso-horyuji.order_jp: 奈良ランチを ひとつ お願いします
hiraso-horyuji.order_romaji: Nara ranchi o hitotsu onegai shimasu
hiraso-horyuji.order_why: Kakinoha-zushi is cured fish pressed onto vinegared rice and wrapped in a persimmon leaf. It began in Yoshino, far from the coast, as a way to keep sea fish. It was a home dish there before Hiraso, founded in 1861, began selling it. Hiraso calls itself sōhonke (the original house) as the first to sell it. The dish itself is older. The set lets you eat it as a meal.
hiraso-horyuji.order_backup: The plain kakinoha-zushi set: three mackerel, two salmon, and a clear soup. ⚑ Unwrap the leaf and leave it on the plate; it is not eaten. Its tannin keeps the fish fresh and takes away the fishy smell.

matsumotoya-horyuji.order_how: Table service, no reservation needed. A large dining hall for coach tours at the Hōryū-ji gate, with a quieter dining room and café beside it, so you will get a table. 💴 Bring cash: JCB is the only card it lists, and it lists no Visa, Mastercard, e-money or QR. ⚠ It has no weekly closing day but closes on irregular days, so it may be shut.
matsumotoya-horyuji.order: Kaki udon: the shop's own udon, with persimmon worked into the dough. Served hot or cold.
matsumotoya-horyuji.order_jp: 柿うどんを ひとつ お願いします
matsumotoya-horyuji.order_romaji: Kaki udon o hitotsu onegai shimasu
matsumotoya-horyuji.order_why: Hōryū-ji is linked with persimmons by Shiki's haiku, the best-known Japanese poem about eating one: he bites a persimmon as the temple bell rings. The shop quotes the haiku on its own pages and has built several persimmon dishes on it. The noodles are its own recipe, and it sells packs of them to take home.
matsumotoya-horyuji.order_backup: Kaki zaru udon: the same noodles served cold, if the walk down from the temple was warm. Persimmon soft-serve for dessert.

katsui-yamanobe.order_how: Sit-down restaurant with table service, on the walking road. Allow time for a full meal.
katsui-yamanobe.order: Hamburg steak set (¥1,800): a minced-beef patty with rice, soup and side dishes.
katsui-yamanobe.order_jp: ハンバーグステーキ定食を ひとつ お願いします
katsui-yamanobe.order_romaji: Hanbāgu sutēki teishoku o hitotsu onegai shimasu
katsui-yamanobe.order_why: Yōshoku is Japan's own version of European cooking, more than a century old, and hamburg steak is its central dish. This kitchen also serves black wagyū beef (kuroge wagyū) and beef stew at several times the price, so it takes its beef seriously. The hamburg set is the cheapest way into a serious menu.
katsui-yamanobe.order_backup: Fried prawn set (エビフライ定食): ¥1,800 for three prawns, ¥2,400 for five. To spend more: the grilled wagyū set (¥2,400).

picton-yanagimoto.order_how: Small canteen inside Yanagimoto station, run by the same company as Katsui, the Western-style restaurant at the Trail Center. Simple and quick. ⚠ Closed Mondays and Tuesdays.
picton-yanagimoto.order: Today's set. The board by the counter is the menu.
picton-yanagimoto.order_jp: 本日のおすすめを ひとつ お願いします
picton-yanagimoto.order_romaji: Honjitsu no osusume o hitotsu onegai shimasu
picton-yanagimoto.order_why: A hot meal at the station for people walking the Yamanobe-no-michi. Come for the location and the opening hours; the food is plain. The same company runs four places, Katsui at the Trail Center among them.
picton-yanagimoto.order_backup: If your train is soon, ask for whatever is quickest. The Japanese order line asks for today's recommendation, which is the safest thing to order in any canteen.

denbe-kibune.order_how: No reservations; you are seated in order of arrival. 🔴 Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR. ⚠ It opens at 11:00 or 11:30, depending on the day, and closes when the soba runs out. Eat when you get there; don't plan to come back later. In November you eat indoors: the riverside platforms in the photos are summer only.
denbe-kibune.order: Soba. It has been the whole menu since 2022, and the choices change with the season. Read the day's list at the counter.
denbe-kibune.order_jp: おそばを ひとつ お願いします
denbe-kibune.order_why: Kibune is a narrow, cold valley of shrine and river. Most of its restaurants serve expensive kaiseki courses for summer visitors who eat on the river platforms. Denbe stays plain and reasonably priced all year. A hot bowl suits the valley, which is cold in November.
denbe-kibune.order_backup: Soba is all there is, and the day's list is short. If your choice has sold out, try Kibune Club, the café 1 min up the lane.

kibune-club.order_how: Café in a wooden building in the valley, serving hot drinks and light meals. Quieter than the soba shops on the lane, and a good place to sit down and warm up. ⚑ Order a meal: if you are here, the soba shop down the lane could not seat you, so this is your lunch. The food menu runs October to May only: four dishes, ¥1,300–2,200.
kibune-club.order: Kyō-yuba gohan, about ¥1,550: sheets of tofu skin with wheat gluten and fish cake in broth, over rice. It comes with red miso soup, a small side dish and pickles.
kibune-club.order_jp: 京湯葉御飯を ひとつ お願いします
kibune-club.order_romaji: Kyō-yuba gohan o hitotsu onegai shimasu
kibune-club.order_why: Yuba is the skin lifted off simmering soy milk, and one of the few dishes that really are from Kyoto. It arrives hot. It is not cooked from raw like the kamameshi, so it comes without a wait.
kibune-club.order_backup: The house speciality is wild boar, three ways: inoshishi kamameshi (boar and rice cooked in its own pot) ¥2,200, a boar and egg-yolk rice bowl ¥1,700, or boar curry ¥1,300 (a limited number each day). ⚠ Think twice about the kamameshi: it is cooked from raw and takes about 20 min. If you are here, you are already running late, and last order is 16:00. If you only want to sit down: matcha and cake sets from ¥1,280. ⚑ Only one listing shows this food menu, so treat all four prices as approximate.

suzuriishitei.order_how: Teahouse on the stone steps, about half way between Takao-bashi bridge and the Jingo-ji gate. 🔴 Cash only: no cards, electronic money or QR. Jingo-ji’s entry is cash too. Order at the counter, then sit on the benches out front.
suzuriishitei.order: Yuba soba: buckwheat noodles in hot broth, topped with sheets of yuba (tofu skin), a Kyoto ingredient.
suzuriishitei.order_jp: 湯葉そばを ひとつ お願いします
suzuriishitei.order_romaji: Yuba soba o hitotsu onegai shimasu
suzuriishitei.order_why: Suzuriishi-tei stands half way up the Jingo-ji steps, beside the inkstone rock (suzuri-ishi) that gives it its name. You pass its door on the way up and again on the way down. A hot bowl suits a November day in the mountains. Yuba is the skin skimmed off simmering soy milk, and it is one of the few truly Kyoto foods you can order here.
suzuriishitei.order_backup: ⚑ The shop is best known for momiji-mochi (a maple-leaf rice cake) with matcha. Order that instead if you want a 10-minute stop rather than a meal.

takao-chaya.order_how: Teahouse on the Jingo-ji steps, above the river. Order at the counter. If the benches are full, they will pack the food to take away. 🔴 No cards or electronic money. A QR payment app is the only cashless option, so carry cash unless you use one.
takao-chaya.order: Momiji udon with yuzu (柚子入もみじうどん): udon made in the shop, in hot broth. The soba version costs the same.
takao-chaya.order_jp: もみじうどんを ひとつ お願いします
takao-chaya.order_romaji: Momiji udon o hitotsu onegai shimasu
takao-chaya.order_why: The udon and the rice cakes are made in the shop, and firm noodles are what the house is proud of. A hot bowl suits a cold November day on the way down from the temple.
takao-chaya.order_backup: Everything on the menu is a momiji (maple) dish. For a fuller meal: two-colour soba (mugwort and plum) with seasonal rice. For a 10-minute stop: matcha with the house momiji-mochi.

yakko-yoshino.order_how: Persimmon-leaf sushi restaurant directly in front of Kinpusen-ji. Table service, 63 seats at tables and on tatami, no reservations. 🔴 Treat it as cash only. Its two listings name two different card brands, and neither is Visa or Mastercard.
yakko-yoshino.order: Kakinoha-zushi — salt-cured mackerel or salmon pressed on vinegared rice and wrapped in a persimmon leaf.
yakko-yoshino.order_jp: 柿の葉寿司を ひとつ お願いします
yakko-yoshino.order_why: The fish is cured in salt, and only the rice is vinegared. The persimmon leaf keeps the sushi fresh and gives it its scent. Unwrap it and leave the leaf: it is not eaten. ⚑ The trip's Hōryū-ji day also has this dish, from the house founded in 1861 that first sold it as a product. This is the mountain-village version, made in Yoshino itself.
yakko-yoshino.order_backup: Kuzu udon: noodles in a broth thickened with Yoshino arrowroot until it turns glossy. It is the local speciality, and the warmer choice on a ridge in November. ⚑ You can order both: eat the udon here, and take the sushi with you, since it keeps.

harukaze-yoshino.order_how: Plain eating house on the Yoshino ridge road, with table service. It takes cards, which Yakko, a few doors along, may not. ⚑ It has 66 seats inside and 6 on a terrace, more than Yakko, so if Yakko has a queue, this place may have none.
harukaze-yoshino.order: Kuzu udon — udon in a broth thickened with Yoshino arrowroot starch, which turns it glossy and holds the heat.
harukaze-yoshino.order_jp: 葛うどんを ひとつ お願いします
harukaze-yoshino.order_romaji: Kuzu udon o hitotsu onegai shimasu
harukaze-yoshino.order_why: Yoshino is known across the region for its kuzu (arrowroot). Kuzu is usually eaten as a sweet. Thickening a hot broth with it is the local savoury way to eat it. A thickened broth stays hot longer than a clear one, which helps after a cold ridge walk.
harukaze-yoshino.order_backup: Kakinoha-zushi, the persimmon-leaf sushi Yoshino is also known for, is sold here too.

tsukumo-udon.order_how: 🔴 Ticket machine at the front of the shop: buy your ticket first, then hand it over at the counter. The shop lists cards, Suica and QR payment, but it is not confirmed that the machine takes them, so carry cash. Udon shop on the second basement floor (B2) of Kyoto Station, at the east exit. 35 seats: 21 at the counter, 14 at tables. ⚑ Open 07:00–22:00, last order 21:30, with no closing day, so it is still open when a day out runs late.
tsukumo-udon.machine_src: Machine in front of the shop: kyotopi.jp/articles/g4Vbp snippet. Label 鶏卵カレーうどん: kyotopi.jp/articles/0CJFD (2024-02-23). Read 2026-09-21. The old card said "Order at the counter".
tsukumo-udon.order: Keiran curry udon (鶏卵カレーうどん), the shop's signature bowl: its own udon in a curry broth, with egg stirred through.
tsukumo-udon.order_jp: 鶏卵カレーうどんを ひとつ お願いします
tsukumo-udon.order_romaji: Keiran karē udon o hitotsu onegai shimasu
tsukumo-udon.order_why: The broth under the curry is drawn slowly and cold from Kujūkushima iriko (dried sardines) and Rishiri kombu (kelp), then finished with a second iriko from the Inland Sea. The udon is made in the shop.
tsukumo-udon.order_backup: ⚑ If you don't want curry, ask for the same bowl without it: keiran udon (鶏卵うどん), egg in the plain iriko broth. It is the way to taste the broth itself. ⚠ Only the curry version is named on the shop's listings, so you may have to ask for the plain one, and it may not be available. Cold choices: tempura zaru udon, with chicken or vegetable tempura. After 17:00 there is a beer set: a glass of beer with chicken, sweet potato and chikuwa (fish cake) tempura.

ekibenya-matsuri.order_how: Ekiben shop: take a box off the shelf, queue at the till, and pay with Suica or a card. You don't need to say anything, and nothing is cooked to order. If no chopsticks are handed over, ask: 「お箸をください」 (o-hashi o kudasai, "chopsticks, please").
ekibenya-matsuri.order: Any box you like. About 150 kinds from all over Japan, restocked through the day.
ekibenya-matsuri.order_jp: これを ひとつ お願いします
ekibenya-matsuri.order_why: About 150 kinds of regional boxed lunches from all over Japan, brought in and restocked through the day. A good pick is one from a place you are going to or have been.
ekibenya-matsuri.order_backup: The phrase above is for pointing at a box behind glass. If a box can be heated, staff may ask atatamemasu ka (温めますか, "Shall I heat it?"). Yes is hai (はい).

ekibenya-odori.order_how: Small ekiben shop on the same passage as Ekibenya Matsuri, next to it. Walk on past the stairs down to platforms 7–8: it faces the Tōkaidō–Sanyō Shinkansen central transfer gate. Take a box and pay at the till; cards and Suica accepted. ⚑ It stocks only the ten best-selling boxes. It is the quicker stop when Ekibenya Matsuri is busy and your train leaves soon.
ekibenya-odori.order: Any box you like, from the ten best-sellers.
ekibenya-odori.order_jp: これを ひとつ お願いします
ekibenya-odori.order_why: The operator stocks it with the ten best-selling boxes instead of the full national range.
ekibenya-odori.order_backup: ⚑ Buy your box before you pass through the Shinkansen transfer gate. Both ekiben shops are outside it.

yumehyakusen-ekie.order_how: Bento and souvenir counter in the souvenir hall on the 2nd floor of ekie at Hiroshima Station. It is a shop with no seating: take a box and pay at the till. 🔴 It is outside the ticket gates, so buy before you go through. Once you are inside, you can't come back to it.
yumehyakusen-ekie.order: Anago-meshi (あなごめし): grilled conger eel laid over rice cooked in the eel's stock. Look for the box from Ueno, a shop in Miyajimaguchi.
yumehyakusen-ekie.order_jp: あなごめしを ひとつ お願いします
yumehyakusen-ekie.order_en: One anago-meshi (conger eel on rice), please.
yumehyakusen-ekie.order_why: Anago-meshi is the local dish of the Hiroshima coast. Ueno has sold this box since 1901, when it started as the station bento for the Miyajima line. It is named after Miyajima, the island you visit on Nov 8, the day before this lunch.
yumehyakusen-ekie.order_backup: ⚠ The anago-meshi box is delivered from Miyajimaguchi and can sell out. If it has: take any other box in the hall. Buy by about 12:30 for the 12:43 train.

ethiopia-akihabara.order_how: Table service. 🔴 Staff ask two things. Spice level: say 3 — san-bai (3ばい); the scale runs 0 (medium) to 70, and 3 is hot. A drink: the line above says no thanks; leave off its last sentence if you want one. Steamed potatoes come free with the curry, with refills.
ethiopia-akihabara.order: Chicken curry (チキンカリー): a thin curry made with 12 spices, with vegetables and beans cooked into the sauce.
ethiopia-akihabara.order_jp: チキンカリーを 3ばいで お願いします。ドリンクは大丈夫です
ethiopia-akihabara.order_romaji: Chikin karī o san-bai de onegai shimasu. Dorinku wa daijōbu desu
ethiopia-akihabara.order_en: Chicken curry, spice level 3, please. No drink, thanks.
ethiopia-akihabara.order_why: Ethiopia has made this curry in Jinbōchō since 1988, and it is a benchmark for Japanese-style spice curry. The 12 spices give it depth even at the low spice levels.
ethiopia-akihabara.order_backup: Other curries: beef, greens, prawn, bean. The bean curries (including chicken-and-bean and greens-and-bean) are never milder than level 3. No pork. The shop also serves European-style roux curries. ⚠ The scale goes past 70 on request — don't.

fukokuen-horyuji.order_how: Table service in a 130-year-old house. There is an English menu. Cards, e-money and QR are accepted. ⚑ Lunch is served 11:00–14:00 only. After that, until 16:00, it serves cake and coffee. ⚠ 39 seats, and it fills between 12:00 and 13:00. If it is full: put your name down and wait in the garden, or walk on to Hiraso, the kakinoha-zushi house 400 m west, on your way to the station.
fukokuen-horyuji.order: Ikaruga tatsuta-age lunch (斑鳩名物竜田揚げランチ): chicken marinated in shio-kōji (salted rice malt) and fried. It comes with the house's wholemeal Miwa sōmen noodles in broth with Yoshino shiitake, and small seasonal dishes.
fukokuen-horyuji.order_jp: 竜田揚げランチを ひとつ お願いします
fukokuen-horyuji.order_romaji: Tatsuta-age ranchi o hitotsu onegai shimasu
fukokuen-horyuji.order_why: Tatsuta-age, soy-marinated fried chicken, is Ikaruga's local dish, and the town promotes it. It is named after the Tatsuta river: the speckled coating is said to look like the river's autumn maple leaves. The house makes its own wholemeal Miwa sōmen with a producer in Miwa, the village where the Oct 30 walk ends. The building was the retirement house of a Meiji-era judicial official. From 1954 it was the town's wedding hall.
fukokuen-horyuji.order_backup: You can ask for ordinary Miwa sōmen instead of the wholemeal noodles. Other sets: a cold pork-shabu salad, and a smaller one-dish lunch. The roast beef lunch must be booked a day ahead, so you cannot order it on the day.

anagomeshi-ueno.order_how: 32 seats, no reservations to eat in. Open 09:00–19:00 every day of the year, last order 18:30. ⚠ It queues: this is the best-known anago restaurant in the Miyajima area, and an hour’s wait at the lunchtime opening is normal. Late afternoon is the best time to try.
anagomeshi-ueno.order: Anago-meshi (あなごめし): conger eel grilled and laid over rice.
anagomeshi-ueno.order_jp: あなごめしを ひとつ お願いします
anagomeshi-ueno.order_en: One anago-meshi (conger eel on rice), please.
anagomeshi-ueno.order_why: Ueno has sold anago-meshi at Miyajimaguchi station since 1901. It is 2 min from the mainland ferry terminal and takes orders until 18:30, two hours after Hayashi’s last order. So if you come down from Misen very late, this is the anago restaurant you can still reach.
anagomeshi-ueno.order_backup: 🔴 If you eat here at about 17:45, skip the okonomiyaki dinner in Hiroshima: you will not manage both. If you came down late and missed lunch, eat here and drop the dinner.

meals.time_hint: Any time this evening. First choice: curry, no queue. Backup: highly rated ramen, but usually a queue.

restaurants.note: Inside Atre Akihabara 1 at the station, 150 m from the hotel — no need to go outside. Open to 22:30, last order 22:00. Table service, 26 seats, no reservations. Cards and IC accepted. If there is a queue, come back later — last order is 22:00. ⚠ No closing day of its own: it closes when Atre does.

Highly rated ramen shop, 1 min from the station. It is the backup only because there is usually a queue: about 10 people, 15–20 min on a normal evening. Look at the door and decide. Dinner 18:00–21:30 (one listing says 21:00). If there is a queue: Ethiopia Curry, 150 m away, or Kamayoshi (udon), 10 min the other way.

meals.time_hint: In Akihabara, on the way back to the hotel.

restaurants.note: Tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet) restaurant, 6 min from the hotel. Open until 21:00, last order 20:00. ⚠ The shop has no website or social account, so its hours can't be confirmed before the trip. If it is closed: go to the backup, Kamayoshi.

Udon shop, 8 min on foot from Marugo. 🔴 Last order 20:00, the same as Marugo. If you are in the queue at Marugo and want to switch, leave by about 19:00. After 19:00, go instead to Ethiopia Curry Kitchen (エチオピア) in Atre Akihabara: last order 22:00, 150 m from the hotel, on the way back.

days.subtitle: the Tokyo splurge, or the late museums and a curry

meals.time_hint: On the way home, along Ueno-Hirokōji

restaurants.note: Yōshoku restaurant (Japanese-style Western food) on Ueno-Hirokōji, on the way home. Last order 19:45. 🔴 On Saturdays both Ueno museums are open until 20:00. If you stay at the museums until they close, you will miss Ponta's last order: eat at Delhi instead (last order 21:30).

Curry shop on the same Ueno-Hirokōji block as Ponta Honke, on the way home. Last order 21:30, so eat here if you stay at the museums until 20:00. ⚑ Delhi is also the first choice for dinner tomorrow (Sunday). If you eat here tonight, have Sunday dinner at Mendokoro Honda instead.

meals.time_hint: Any time this evening. Both places are near the hotel.

restaurants.note: Curry restaurant, 10 min on foot from the hotel. ⚑ If you ate here last night (Saturday's dinner backup, if you stayed late at the Ueno museums), eat at Mendokoro Honda (ramen) tonight instead.

Highly rated ramen shop, 150 m from the hotel. It has 18 seats and they free up slowly, so there is usually a queue of about 10 on a normal evening. Look at the door and decide: if there is a queue, eat at Delhi instead.

days.subtitle: something easy, on the way home

meals.time_hint: At the summit, roughly 12:30–13:30

restaurants.note: ⛔ Buy onigiri or sandwiches at a konbini in Akihabara before you board the train, and eat them on the summit deck. No teahouse on the mountain publishes a calendar of closing days, so a hot meal up there is a bonus if one is open. The two summit teahouses are open 10:00–15:00. On the way up are Jūitchōme-chaya (last order 15:00) and Gongen-jaya (open to 16:00). 🔴 Takahashiya, at the foot of the mountain, serves tororo soba (soba with grated yam) until last order 16:30. 16:30 is also when you need to be at the tsukemen shop in Shinjuku for dinner, so eating soba here means skipping that dinner.

meals.time_hint: 🔴 If you can reach the tsukemen shop in Shinjuku by 16:30: eat there. Later: curry in Akihabara, by the hotel.

restaurants.note: Prawn tsukemen shop in Shinjuku, 14 counter seats. ⛔ Be at the door by about 16:30. If you can't make it, eat at Ethiopia Curry in Akihabara instead. Before 16:30 there is no wait. Just after 17:00 the queue is out on the street, and at 19:25 the wait is 35 min. You can decide on the platform at Takaosanguchi. If the descent goes to plan, you reach Shinjuku at about 16:00 and walk straight in. A slow descent, soba at Takahashiya or a long stop at the summit will make you too late. ⚠ The nearest stations are Shinjuku-sanchōme and Shinjuku-gyoenmae, not JR Shinjuku. Allow more than 4 min for the walk: your legs will be tired after three hours on the mountain.

Curry restaurant in Atre at Akihabara station, 150 m from the hotel and on your way home. 🔴 Take this one if you come off the mountain later than planned. Open until 22:30, last order 22:00. Table service, 26 seats. Cards and IC accepted. You don't have to decide before you board: if you reach Shinjuku after about 16:30, stay on the train.

restaurants.cuisine: Indian street food and spice curry
restaurants.note: Indian street food and spice curry, about 10 min on foot from the Keiō concourse in Shinjuku. ⛔ Closed 15:00–17:00, which is when you are likely to reach Shinjuku. So it is no help if the tsukemen shop has a queue at that time. People queue before it reopens at 17:00, and you can't know in advance how long the wait will be. ✅ Cards, IC and QR accepted. It is the cashless choice in Shinjuku; lunch and the tsukemen shop are both cash only. Use it only if you are eating at 17:30 or later and will accept a queue of any length.

days.subtitle: late lunch in Kamakura, easy supper near the hotel

meals.time_hint: Late lunch, about 15:00, after Tsurugaoka Hachimangū — 3 min from Kamakura Station east exit

restaurants.note: Open 11:00–20:00 with no afternoon break, last order 19:00. Closed Wednesdays (today is Tuesday). 🔴 Cash only. Shirasu bowl ¥1,430 · large-prawn tempura bowl ¥2,100 · house tempura bowl ¥3,500. Raw shirasu depends on that morning's catch; the boiled one is always on.

meals.time_hint: Back in Akihabara, any time before 22:00

restaurants.note: Atre Akihabara 1, 150 m from the hotel. Last order 22:00. Same place as night 1.

meals.time_hint: Buy at Tokyo Station 08:45–09:00; eat on the 09:30 Nozomi at about 11:00–11:35

restaurants.note: Ekiben (boxed lunch) hall at Tokyo Station. ⚑ It is inside the ordinary JR gates, before the Tōkaidō Shinkansen transfer gate. Arriving from Akihabara on the Yamanote line, you are already inside the gates and walk right past its door. Buy your box before you pass the Shinkansen gate.
Smaller ekiben counter next to Ekibenya Matsuri, directly opposite the Shinkansen central transfer gate. It is also on the outside of that gate.

meals.time_hint: Any time this evening, near the hotel. Tonight is the only one of the ten Kyoto nights with no fixed dinner time.

restaurants.note: Sukiyaki restaurant in Eat Paradise, the restaurant floor on the 11th floor of JR Kyoto Isetan, 147 m from the platforms and indoors all the way. Last entry and last order 21:00. There is a queue for the floor 18:00–19:00; after 19:00 you can usually walk in. ⛔ No IC cards or QR payment: pay by card or cash. ⚠ It closes on the department store's closing days. The store's schedule lists none through December, but a closure on an ordinary Wednesday cannot be ruled out. If the store is closed, Kyoto Yamaroku, the backup grilled-fish restaurant in the Isetan basement, is closed too.

Ramen shop, 5 min on foot from the hotel. Open until 01:00, later than any other Kyoto dinner on this trip. ⚑ Another Kyoto shop with the same name is at Sanjō-Kawaramachi. Check the sign: this is the main shop (honten), at Higashi-Shiokōji Mukaihata-chō 845.

meals.time_hint: After the Yumedono, ideally closer to 13:00 than noon. Nishinokyō, the next stop, has nowhere to eat.

restaurants.cuisine: Ikaruga tatsuta-age and Nara set lunches
restaurants.note: Café-restaurant in an old house, 3–4 min south-east of the Yumedono, where the temple visit ends. ⚑ Come after 13:00 if you can. Lunch is served until 14:00, there are only 39 seats, and 12:00–13:00 is when it fills and people wait. The shop takes no bookings for that hour. If it is full: Hiraso and Matsumotoya are 400 m west, on your way to the station. The walk to the station is the same length from all three.

Shop and restaurant selling kakinoha-zushi (sushi wrapped in persimmon leaves), on the street leading to the temple gate, open every day of the year. The shop is open 10:00–16:00, but the dining room serves 11:00–15:00 (last order). So a sit-down lunch after 13:00 is still fine. Nara lunch set ¥2,200, plain set ¥1,500.

restaurants.cuisine: Country cooking, udon and persimmon dishes
restaurants.note: Large dining hall for coach tours, 2 min past Hiraso on the street to Hōryū-ji's gate. It is very unlikely to be full. ⚠ It closes on irregular days and publishes no schedule, so it may be shut. 💴 Bring cash: the only card it takes is JCB.

meals.time_hint: Near the hotel. You are back at Kyoto Station around 18:00.

restaurants.note: Griddle restaurant serving manbo-yaki, Kyoto's own style of okonomiyaki, open since 1948. Last order 21:30. ⚠ Closed Wednesdays and on the third Thursday of the month; today is neither. Closure news is posted only on its Instagram account, manbo_2020: check it the day before you go.

Ramen shop 5–8 min from the hotel, on the west side of the station. Open from 07:00 with no break, last order 21:30, so at 18:00 there are hours of service left. 11 seats, no reservations. If there is a queue, walk away and come back later. ⚠ It closes on irregular days and publishes no schedule you can check in advance.

meals.time_hint: On the walk. You reach the Tenri City Trail Center at about 11:50–12:40

restaurants.note: Western-style restaurant (yōshoku) inside the Tenri City Trail Center, on the walking road just past Chōgaku-ji. ⚠ The menu changes at 14:00, and set meals stop at 15:30, an hour before the 16:30 close. ⚑ A third option, after this and the station canteen at Yanagimoto: buy a konbini picnic in Tenri before you start, in the shopping arcade the walk begins in.
Canteen inside Yanagimoto station, 20 min (about 1 km) west of the Trail Center, downhill off the walking road. Open 10:00–15:00. If you end the walk early, you can eat here and catch your train.

meals.time_hint: Near the hotel. You get back to Kyoto Station at about 17:30–18:30

restaurants.note: Clam-broth ramen shop, 5–8 min from the hotel, on the west side of the station. 11 seats, no reservations. Open 07:00–22:00 with no midday break, last order 21:30, so arriving at 17:30–18:30 leaves you 3–4 hours. ⚠ Some visitors report hour-long waits. If there is a queue, walk away and come back later. ⚠ It closes on irregular days and does not publish them anywhere you can read.
Okonomiyaki restaurant, 10 min on foot (700 m) from the Hachijō exit on the south side of Kyoto Station. Last order 22:15. ⚠ It can be full on a busy night: walk in early in the evening.

meals.time_hint: In Nara at about 12:30, straight after the exhibition. The arcade is 10 min west; the hillside halls come after lunch.

restaurants.note: Curry restaurant in the Mochiidono covered arcade, 10–12 min west of the museum. 🔴 No midday break: last entry 19:25, last order 19:30. Every plate is made to order, so nothing sells out. ⚑ 2 min further along: Menya K (麺屋K), an 11-seat ramen counter on the Ramen WEST Hyakumeiten list ("100 famous ramen shops, west Japan"). It closes when it sells out, but at 12:45 it is probably still serving. If there is no queue, it is worth choosing over the curry. Nothing depends on it.

restaurants.cuisine: Kamameshi — rice cooked to order over a flame
restaurants.note: Kamameshi restaurant in Nara Park, by the museum entrance. It is the only lunch choice today that is not in the arcades. ⚠ At 12:30 on a busy Saturday expect a queue: walk on unless the door is clear. 🔴 Last order 16:00 (the shop closes later). By 15:00 the queue is gone, so it works if you come down from the hillside hungry instead of eating at midday. Its one irregular October closure is the 19th, so it is open on the 31st.

meals.time_hint: Near the hotel. You are back at Kyoto Station about 18:40 on the 17:44 Kintetsu express from Nara.

restaurants.note: Ramen shop 5 min from the hotel, open until 01:00, so you cannot arrive too late tonight. ⚑ Or eat in Nara before the train: Tori-soba Zagin, 105 m from Kintetsu Nara station on the Konishi-dōri arcade. Saturday 11:00–21:00, last order 20:30, walk-in only, no closing day. The day's sightseeing ends in daylight, so there is time, and your evening in Kyoto is then free. Decide on the day.

Okonomiyaki restaurant, 10 min (700 m) on foot from the Hachijō exit of Kyoto Station, the exit on the Kintetsu side. Last order 22:15. On the 17:44 express you reach the station about 18:40, with hours to spare. ⛔ Cash only: carry notes. Walk in; arrive early in the evening for the best chance of a seat.

meals.time_hint: On the Kibune lane, after the walk over the ridge from Kurama

restaurants.note: Soba shop on the Kibune lane. ⚠ It closes when the soba runs out; there is no fixed closing time. A Sunday at the peak of autumn is the busiest day on this lane. If it is closed or sold out, there are two more options. Kokon Fujiya (古今藤や), at the Sanbon-sugi stop on the 30–40 min walk down to Kibuneguchi, is open 11:00–21:00. Its café menu needs no reservation: matcha sweets and warabimochi, a snack only. After that, eat at Demachiyanagi around 14:00. You change trains there on the way to Sanjūsangen-dō, and there are plenty of places to eat with no closing time to worry about. At worst you eat an hour later, in the city.

restaurants.cuisine: Yuba rice, wild boar and cake sets
restaurants.note: Café 1 min up the lane from Denbe (the soba shop). Last order 16:00. ⚑ From October to May it serves a food menu as well as sweets, so in November you can have lunch here: four dishes, ¥1,300–2,200. ⚠ Closing days are irregular and announced only on its Instagram. On 17 October the profile still said it was closed for the summer and would reopen in the autumn, with no date. It may be closed.

meals.time_hint: Near the hotel. You are back at Kyoto Station around 17:15–17:45

restaurants.cuisine: Saikyō-yaki — miso-cured grilled fish set meals
restaurants.note: Grilled-fish restaurant in the basement of the Isetan at Kyoto Station. Dinner 16:00–20:00, last order 19:30. No reservations: take a numbered ticket at the door. It has 21 seats, so you may have to wait between 18:00 and 19:00. ⚠ It closes on the department store's closing days, as does the sukiyaki restaurant Morita-ya, 11 floors up in the same building. The store's schedule, updated 1 October, lists no closing day for Yamaroku through December. The backup tonight, Kubota, is in a different building.

Miso tsukemen shop at Gojō, one stop from Kyoto Station on the Karasuma subway, or about 13 min on foot. ⚑ Evening service starts at 18:00. You are back at Kyoto Station around 17:15–17:45, so expect to wait a little. Last order 21:30. ⚠ Its listings disagree about its closing day, so it may be closed.

meals.time_hint: Near Kyoto Station: you are back at the station about 17:05

restaurants.note: Okonomiyaki restaurant (Kyoto beta-yaki style), 700 m and 10 min on foot from the Hachijō exit on the south side of Kyoto Station. Open 17:00–23:00, last order 22:15. You are back at the station about 17:05, so you reach the door about 17:15: walk in then. It is often full: walk-ins are usually offered a seat for 90 minutes only, even right at opening, and 90 minutes is enough for this meal. ⛔ If no seat is offered at all: go to the backup, Yamamoto Mambo, another beta-yaki okonomiyaki restaurant. ⛔ Cash only. Yamamoto Mambo is cash only too, so tonight you can't pay by card anywhere.

Griddle restaurant serving manbo-yaki, Kyoto's own style of okonomiyaki, open since 1948. Last order 21:30. ⚠ Closed Wednesdays and on the third Thursday of the month; today is neither. Closure news is posted only on its Instagram account, manbo_2020: check it the day before you go.

meals.time_hint: 12:50–13:40, at a teahouse half way down the Jingo-ji steps, before you reach the bridge and the river road north to Saimyō-ji

restaurants.cuisine: Mountain teahouse — soba, udon and yudōfu
restaurants.note: Teahouse half way up the Jingo-ji steps, so you pass it on the way up and again on the way down. If the benches are full on the way up, eat there on the way down instead. Open every day in November. Autumn set: yudōfu (simmered tofu), a simmered dish, seasoned rice, momiji tempura (fried maple leaves) and pickles, ¥1,900. ⚠ In autumn the house momiji-mochi (maple-leaf rice cake) may not be served between 11:00 and 14:00, so have the soba and take the mochi only if it is available. ⚠ Today is a national holiday in Takao’s maple season, so expect crowds. Lunch does not limit the day. Kōzan-ji’s 17:00 close does.

restaurants.cuisine: Momiji sets, matcha and house-made noodles
restaurants.note: Teahouse on the Jingo-ji steps, about 50 m from Suzuriishi-tei and at about the same height, so you can check both in one stop. ⚠ It closes on irregular days. It is reported to stay open every day from October to early December, but the shop publishes nothing itself, so this is not certain. If both teahouses are full or closed: Yamamoto Shokudō (山本食堂, a diner) at the main Takao bus stop is open 09:00 to about 18:00, every day in the season. A queue at the teahouses does not affect it. Togano-chaya (とがの茶屋, a teahouse) at Kōzan-ji is open 09:00–17:00, every day from 20 October to 30 November. It is a late-afternoon snack stop before the bus, not a lunch place. Useful because you may wait 10–20 min for the bus at Toganoo.

meals.time_hint: Near the hotel. Back at Kyoto Station about 17:55 on the 16:54 bus (if you visit the Daishi-dō), or 17:11 on the 16:14 bus. Both are just before the holiday dinner rush.

restaurants.note: Sukiyaki restaurant in Eat Paradise, the restaurant floor on the 11th floor of the JR Kyoto Isetan department store. It is 147 m from the platforms, indoors all the way. Last entry and last order are both 21:00. The floor has queues from about 18:00 to 19:00. ⚑ Department stores open on holidays, so it is open today. ⛔ Its own page says it does not take electronic money (IC cards such as Suica) or QR payment. Pay by card or cash. Open every day through December. ⚠ The backup ramen shop closes on irregular days that it does not publish, so it cannot be checked before the day.

Clam-broth ramen shop, 5–8 min walk from the hotel, on the west side of Kyoto Station. Last order 21:30. ⚠ 11 seats, no reservations, and the queue length is unknown. Tonight is a national holiday early in Takao’s maple season, so Kyoto Station is busier than on a normal Tuesday. Arriving about 17:55 still beats the worst of it. The shop stays open until 22:00 without a break, so if the queue is long you can leave and come back. ⚠ It closes on irregular days, and it publishes them nowhere you can read.

meals.time_hint: At Daigo, about 12:30, before the 13:29 train

restaurants.cuisine: Bento or onigiri bought at Kyoto Station before you leave
restaurants.note: ⚠ Daigo-ji's own restaurant has been closed for renovation since 1 June 2026, and the temple's website gives no reopening date. Do not count on buying food at the temple. Buy a bento or onigiri (rice balls) at Kyoto Porta, the shopping mall under Kyoto Station, before you leave at 08:30. Its food shops open at 07:30. Al Plaza supermarket at Daigo station does not open until 09:30, after you have gone into the temple. Eat in the temple grounds at about 12:30, before the 13:29 train. If you forgot: after the treasure house, walk back to Al Plaza (1 min from Daigo station exit 2), buy lunch there and eat it before the 13:29 train. Do not wait to eat at Fushimi Inari: you arrive about 15:30, and the mountain loop has to start straight away. There is no food on the mountain paths.

meals.time_hint: Near the hotel. You get back to Kyoto Station at about 17:45–18:30 on the train from Inari, earlier if you turn back at Yotsutsuji

restaurants.cuisine: Saikyō-yaki — miso-cured grilled fish set meals
restaurants.note: Grilled-fish restaurant in the basement (B1) of the Isetan department store at Kyoto Station. Dinner 16:00–20:00, last order 19:30. No reservations: you take a numbered ticket at the door. With 21 seats there is likely to be a wait between 18:00 and 19:00, which is when you get back. If people are already waiting, go straight to Honke Daiichi Asahi (ramen, 5 min on foot from the hotel, open until 01:00). It follows the department store's closing days. The store's schedule, updated 1 October 2026, lists no closing day for this shop through December.

Ramen shop, 5 min on foot from the hotel. Open until 01:00, so it is open whenever you get back tonight. Closed Thursdays; today is Wednesday. ⚑ Another Kyoto shop with the same name is at Sanjō-Kawaramachi, with the same Thursday closing day. Check the sign: this is the main shop (honten, 本店), at Higashi-Shiokōji Mukaihata-chō 845.

meals.time_hint: In Naka-senbon, about 11:30–12:15, after Kinpusen-ji and Yoshimizu Shrine and before the climb to Kami-senbon

restaurants.note: Persimmon-leaf sushi restaurant, opposite the Zaō-dō of Kinpusen-ji. 63 seats at tables and on tatami, so you can usually walk in even on a busy autumn day. No table can be booked. ⚠ Carry cash. Its two listings name two different card brands, and neither is Visa or Mastercard. ⚑ Eat lunch on the mountain. The eateries there close at about 16:00–17:00, so lunch is the only meal you can have on the ridge. Dinner is back in Kyoto.

Eating house 30 seconds' walk along the street from Yakko, so it is easy to check both. It has more seats than Yakko, and it takes cards. ⚠ It closes on irregular days and publishes no pattern, so it may be shut today. ⚑ If every restaurant in the village is full: buy a box of persimmon-leaf sushi (kakinoha-zushi) over the counter at Yakko, Tatsumi (たつみ) or Daiyo (醍予). Eat it at the Hanayagura viewpoint on the way up. The sushi is wrapped in leaves and eaten at room temperature, so it carries well. ⚑ A sweet stop, separate from lunch: Nakai Shunpū-dō (中井春風堂), in front of the Zaō-dō, makes kuzumochi and kuzukiri (arrowroot sweets), ¥900 each. Walk in and order. They are made to order, take about 20 min, and must be eaten within 10 min, in the shop. Quantities are limited. If you add this stop, go to lunch at Yakko earlier.

meals.time_hint: Near the hotel. You get back to Kyoto Station at about 17:50 (about 17:30 on the limited express), or 18:15–18:30 if you go up to Oku-senbon, and it may be later

restaurants.note: Clam-broth ramen shop, 5–8 min from the hotel, on the west side of the station. 11 seats, no reservations. Last order 21:30, more than 3 hours after you are due back. ⚠ If there is a queue, walk away and come back later: you have time. ⚠ It closes on irregular days and does not publish them anywhere you can read.

Udon shop inside Kyoto Station, on the second basement floor (B2) at the east exit, 136 m from the hotel. You never go outside, which helps if you get back late and tired. ⚠ Hours: two of its listings say 07:00–22:00, last order 21:30. A third says 06:00–23:00 on weekdays. Plan on the shorter hours.

meals.time_hint: Near the hotel, on your last night in Kyoto. You get back to Kyoto Station at about 17:00–18:00

restaurants.note: Griddle restaurant serving manbo-yaki, Kyoto's own style of okonomiyaki, open since 1948. Last order 21:30. ⚠ Closed Wednesdays and on the third Thursday of the month; today is neither. Closure news is posted only on its Instagram account, manbo_2020: check it the day before you go.

Tsukemen (noodles you dip into a thick miso soup) shop at Gojō: one stop from Kyoto Station on the Karasuma subway, or about 13 min on foot. ⚑ The evening opening is 18:00, so if you get back between 17:00 and 18:00 you may have to wait a while. Last order 21:30. ⚠ Its weekly closing day is not known.

meals.time_hint: Near the station, 12:05–13:05. Leave the bags at the hotel first, after the 11:38 arrival. Shukkei-en at 13:15.

restaurants.note: Okonomiyaki shop, 10 min on foot from the Shinkansen (north) exit, outside the station building. 25 seats. The pancake bases are cooked in advance, so your plate arrives in under 5 min. Most okonomiyaki shops take 15 min. ⚑ Also open for dinner, 17:00–20:30. 🔴 If there is a queue here: walk to Masaru (the backup below), in the same block. Don't go back to the station. The long queues are at the okonomiyaki counters in ekie, the shopping building at Hiroshima Station. Micchan Sōhonten there usually has a 30 min queue at lunch, and about 1 hour if you miss the first sitting. ✅ Micchan is still useful if this shop is closed or you are short of cash. It has 41 seats, takes cards, and is 5 min back at the station. ⚠ The counters in ekie close on the ekie building's closing days, and those are not published far enough ahead to check. If ekie is closed, all of them are. This shop and Masaru are outside the building. Tonight's dinner choice is also inside ekie.

Okonomiyaki counter, 10 min from the Shinkansen (north) exit, in the same block as Icchan and also outside the station building. 🔴 Watch the clock: lunch runs 11:30–14:00, but last order is 13:30. If Icchan has a queue, walk here straight away, so you can order by 13:30. ⚠ All counter seats. Nobody knows how long the wait here usually is, so it may have a queue too. ⛔ Neither lunch place takes credit cards, and neither do the two dinner places. ⚑ Masaru is also tomorrow's dinner choice. You can eat here today and again tomorrow. If you don't want it twice, have tomorrow's dinner at Kunimatsu instead.

meals.time_hint: When the tram from the Peace Park reaches Hiroshima Station, about 18:45–19:00

restaurants.note: Soupless tantanmen counter on the 1st floor of ekie, the shopping building at Hiroshima Station. It is on your way from the tram stop to the hotel. ⛔ Suica-type IC cards and nanaco accepted, but no credit cards. The dinner backup takes cash and PayPay. So there is no way to pay by credit card at either dinner place tonight. ⚠ It has no closing day of its own: it closes when the ekie building does, and ekie's closing days are not published far enough ahead to check. The same goes for the okonomiyaki counters that back up today's lunch, and for Monday's ekiben (station lunch box) counter upstairs. Tonight's backup, Masaru, is outside the building. ⚑ Icchan (today's lunch choice) is also open for dinner tonight, 17:00–20:30, if you want okonomiyaki instead.

Okonomiyaki counter, 10 min from the Shinkansen (north) exit. Dinner runs until 23:00 (last order 22:00). ⚑ If you would rather have okonomiyaki a second time today than tantanmen, Masaru is in Tabelog's Okonomiyaki Hyakumeiten (top 100) list; Kunimatsu is not. It is also tomorrow's dinner choice. If you eat here tonight, have tomorrow's dinner at Kunimatsu instead.

meals.time_hint: 15:00–16:15 on Omotesandō, after you come down from Misen at about 14:45–15:15. The shore walk at dusk comes after lunch

restaurants.note: Oyster and anago restaurant on Omotesandō. Anago-meshi ¥2,900, grilled anago ¥2,700, two anago rice balls (anago-musubi) ¥1,200, plus udon, soba, tonkatsu and fried-prawn sets, so one stop is enough after the climb. 🔴 The anago is on the shop’s SECOND menu card. The first card is all oysters. Last order is 16:30, half an hour before closing, so aim to be seated by about 15:45. You come down at about 14:45, and the walk takes 15 min. ⚠ The shop says its hours can change with the season.

restaurants.cuisine: Anago-meshi — the 1901 house at the ferry terminal
restaurants.note: 🔴 Anago-meshi restaurant on the MAINLAND, 2 min from the Miyajimaguchi ferry terminal. Use it if you come down from the mountain very late: it takes orders until 18:30, two hours after Hayashi’s 16:30 last order. Off the 17:25 ferry you land at 17:35. ⚠ Eating here means giving up the okonomiyaki dinner in Hiroshima, and there is often a queue. If you only want a snack: Momijidō Honten (紅葉堂 本店) on the island’s shopping street, 5 min from the pier, is open until 17:30 and sells fried momiji-manjū (maple-leaf cakes) for ¥190. Momijidō is cash only.

meals.time_hint: Your train reaches Hiroshima Station at 18:20, so you sit down at about 18:30–18:50. One train later: 18:45–19:05. Two trains later: 19:00–19:20

restaurants.note: Okonomiyaki restaurant, 10 min on foot from Hiroshima Station’s north exit. Open until 23:00, last order 22:00, so a later boat or train (the 17:55 ferry, the 18:03 or 18:19 train) costs you nothing. 💴 Cash and PayPay only. Kunimatsu, the backup, does not take credit cards either. ⚑ Saturday’s lunch is okonomiyaki too. If you want okonomiyaki only once, eat at Kunimatsu tonight.

Soupless tantanmen (spicy sesame noodles) counter on the first floor of ekie, the mall inside Hiroshima Station. From the JR train it is 56 m to the counter, and you never leave the building. ⚠ It publishes no closing day: it closes when ekie does, and ekie’s calendar is not published far enough ahead to check. Masaru, the first choice tonight, is outside the building.

meals.time_hint: Bought at ekie between about 11:30 and 12:30, eaten on the 12:43 Nozomi

restaurants.note: Bento and souvenir counter on the 2nd floor of ekie, outside the ticket gates. Look for the sign おみやげ館 (Omiyage-kan, souvenir hall). The anago-meshi box costs about ¥2,430 for the regular size. This is a reported price: the shop doesn't publish one. ⚠ The shop publishes no closing day of its own. It closes on the days the ekie building closes.

restaurants.cuisine: Ekiben — six counters inside the Shinkansen gates
restaurants.note: ⛔ Skip Musashi (むさし 広島駅新幹線弁当工房). It is the best-known bento shop at this station, and it closes every Monday. Today is a Monday. The other five ekiben counters inside the Shinkansen gates are open, so you will find a boxed lunch even if the anago-meshi box has sold out. Hiroshima Ekiben (廣島驛辨當), in the Meihinkan zone, 05:30–21:30. The sign to look for is 銘品館 (Meihinkan). A second Hiroshima Ekiben counter, on the Tokyo-direction platform, 08:00–20:00. Seven-Eleven Kiosk, on the same platform, 05:35–22:00. ⚑ Kyō no Sushi (鮨処 京の寿し) and Ajiroya (あじろや), both 08:00–20:00, are both counters inside Omiyage Kaidō (おみやげ街道) at the central Shinkansen gate. Omiyage Kaidō is open 06:00–22:00 and has an ATM.

meals.time_hint: 17:30–19:00, whenever you like. You reach the hotel at about 16:55 and nothing is planned after dinner

restaurants.note: Udon shop, 10 min on foot from the hotel and 3 min from Awajichō station. Opens at 17:30. Last order 20:00, 20 min before closing. ⚠ The shop posts its opening days on its own social media account, so don't assume it is open: check first. It also closes early when the noodles run out.

Curry restaurant about 150 m from the hotel, on the 1st floor of Atre Akihabara 1. It is on your walk from Akihabara Station to the hotel, so there is no extra trip. Last order 22:00. Cards and IC accepted; no reservations. Its last order is 2 hours later than at Menso Kamayoshi, the first-choice dinner (20:00). So if the Shinkansen is late, or Kamayoshi is closed that day, you can still eat 150 m from the hotel. ⚠ It publishes no closing day of its own and follows the Atre building's calendar.

meals.time_hint: About 12:30 in Ryōgoku, between the station and the Edo-Tokyo Museum

restaurants.note: Chanko restaurant on the 2nd and 3rd floors, 1 min (103 m) from the east exit of JR Ryōgoku station. Lunch service 11:00–15:00. ⚠ It takes bookings, so it can be full. But it has 120 seats (tables, tatami and sunken hearths), so on an ordinary Tuesday at 12:30 there should be room. ⚑ If this and Chanko Kirishima (the backup) are both full: Sumo Chaya Terao (相撲茶屋 寺尾), 173 m away. It is run by a former wrestler, the elder brother of the wrestler Terao it is named after. ⚠ Its seats, hours and closing day are not known, so it may be closed.

Chanko restaurant inside the Edo NOREN building, 42 m from the west exit of Ryōgoku station. It is in the same block as the Edo-Tokyo Museum, on your way there. Lunch until 15:00, last order 14:00. 88 seats at tables, so like Ami it has room on a busy day. ⚠ The only closing days it publishes are in summer. Whether it closes on any day in November is not known. 🔴 Don't go to the wrong branch: Kirishima's main shop (honten), 97 m away, is closed on Mondays and Tuesdays, so it is closed today.

meals.time_hint: From about 17:30. You are back at Ryōgoku by 16:30–17:15, with or without Kiyosumi garden (it closes at 17:00)

restaurants.note: Tonkatsu (pork cutlet) restaurant on Yokozuna Yokochō, the lane off the east exit of Ryōgoku station. Last order 22:00, so there is still time for dinner after Kiyosumi garden: the garden closes at 17:00, and you are back at Ryōgoku by about 17:15 (earlier if you skip it). ✅ Open every day of the year except over New Year, with no irregular closing days. ⚑ Another choice: Teuchi Ren (手打式 らぁ麺 蓮, a 7-seat ramen shop), 8 min on foot from Ryōgoku station, or 6 min from Morishita station, in the direction of Kiyosumi. Open 17:00–22:00, closed Mondays. 🔴 Go only if there is no queue: it is cash only, and you may not wait inside. This is the last night of the trip, so if it doesn't work out, there is no other night to try again. ⚑ Check the name: the last character is 蓮, not 練. Searching for 練 will not find it.

Ramen shop at Akihabara, 150 m from the hotel: 2 stops (about 4 min) on the Sōbu line from Ryōgoku. Use it if you go straight back to the hotel. ⚠ Dinner opens at 18:00, and you reach Akihabara by about 17:30 even if you visit Kiyosumi garden (it closes at 17:00). So either eat at Hasegawa in Ryōgoku, which is already open, or leave your bag at the hotel and come back here at 18:00. Look at the door and decide: if there is a queue, eat at Ethiopia Curry in Atre Akihabara, 150 m from the hotel, instead.
